title.zh: 卷九十五 列傳第八十三: 蠻 獠 林邑 赤土 真臘 婆利
title.en: Volume 95 Biographies 83: Man, Rao, Linyi, Chi Tu, Khmer, Brunei
title.raw: 卷九十五 列傳第八十三: 蠻 獠 林邑 赤土 真臘 婆利 Volume 95 Biographies 83: Man, Rao, Linyi, Chi Tu, Khmer, Brunei

sentences.zh: 蠻 獠 林邑 赤土 真臘 婆利

translations.literal: Man; Rao; Linyi; Chi Tu; Zhenla; Poli.
translations.idiomatic: Man; Rao; Linyi; Chi Tu; Khmer; Brunei.

sentences.zh: 列傳第八十三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 83.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 83

sentences.zh: 蠻獠林邑赤土真臘婆利

translations.literal: Man, Rao, Linyi, Chi Tu, Zhenla, and Poli.
translations.idiomatic: Man, Rao, Linyi, Chi Tu, Khmer, and Brunei.

sentences.zh: 蠻之種類，蓋盤瓠之後。

translations.literal: The Man tribes are descendants of Panhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Man peoples were said to be descendants of Panhu.

sentences.zh: 在江、淮之間，部落滋蔓，布於數州，東連壽春，西通巴、蜀，北接汝、潁，往往有焉。

translations.literal: Between the Yangtze and Huai, their tribes proliferated and spread across several provinces, reaching Shouchun in the east, Ba and Shu in the west, and Ru and Ying in the north — they were found everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yangtze and Huai their clans multiplied and spread across several provinces, reaching Shouchun to the east, Ba and Shu to the west, and Ru and Ying to the north; they were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 其于魏氏，不甚為患，至晉之末，稍以繁昌，漸為寇暴矣。

translations.literal: Under the Wei they were not much of a problem; by the end of Jin they grew somewhat flourishing and gradually became raiders and plunderers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei they caused little trouble, but by the closing years of Jin they had grown numerous and began to raid and pillage.

sentences.zh: 自劉、石亂後，諸蠻無所忌憚，故其族漸得北遷，陸渾以南，滿于山谷，宛、洛蕭條，略為丘墟矣。

translations.literal: After the turmoil of Liu and Shi, the Man tribes had nothing to fear; thus their people gradually moved north. South of Luhun they filled the valleys; Wan and Luo became desolate, almost ruins.
translations.idiomatic: After the upheavals of the Liu and Shi regimes the Man tribes no longer held back, and their people gradually pushed north. South of Luhun they packed the mountain valleys, while Wan and Luoyang wasted away into near ruin.

sentences.zh: 道武既定中山，聲教被於河表。

translations.literal: After Emperor Daowu secured Zhongshan, his civilizing influence reached the lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Daowu had secured Zhongshan, the reach of his rule extended south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 泰常八年，蠻王梅安率渠帥數千朝京師，求留質子，以表忠款。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taichang, the Man king Mei An led several thousand chieftains to court, asking to leave a hostage prince to show his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taichang the Man king Mei An came to the capital at the head of several thousand chieftains, offering to leave a hostage son as proof of his fealty.

sentences.zh: 始光中，拜安侍子豹為安遠將軍、江州刺史、順陽公。

translations.literal: In the Shiguang era, An's attendant son Bao was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance, Inspector of Jiangzhou, and Duke of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shiguang era the court made Mei An's son Bao, who had served as his attendant, general who pacifies the distance, inspector of Jiangzhou, and duke of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 興光中，蠻王文武龍請降，詔褒慰之，拜南雍州刺史、魯陽侯。

translations.literal: In the Xinguang era, the Man king Wen Wulong asked to surrender; an edict praised and comforted him; he was appointed Inspector of Southern Yongzhou and Marquis of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinguang era the Man king Wen Wulong submitted; the court commended and reassured him and named him inspector of southern Yongzhou and marquis of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 延興中，大陽蠻首桓誕擁沔水以北，滍葉以南，八萬餘落，遣使內屬。

translations.literal: In the Yanxing era, the Dayang Man chieftain Huan Dan held north of the Han River and south of the Zhi and Ye — over eighty thousand households — and sent envoys to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanxing the Dayang Man leader Huan Dan controlled more than eighty thousand households between the Han River to the north and the Zhi and Ye rivers to the south, and sent envoys to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉之，拜誕征南將軍、東荊州刺史、襄陽王，聽自選郡縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was pleased and appointed Dan General Who Conquers the South, Eastern Inspector of Jingzhou, and King of Xiangyang, allowing him to choose his own commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen welcomed this and made Dan general who conquers the south, eastern inspector of Jingzhou, and king of Xiangyang, letting him pick his own counties and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 誕字天生，桓玄之子也。

translations.literal: Dan, styled Tiansheng, was the son of Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Dan, courtesy name Tiansheng, was a son of Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 初，玄西奔至枚迥洲被殺，誕時年數歲，流竄大陽蠻中，遂習其俗。

translations.literal: At first, when Xuan fled west to Meihui Isle and was killed, Dan was only a few years old; he wandered into the Dayang Man and learned their customs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan fled west to Meihui Isle and was killed, Dan was still a small child; he drifted among the Dayang Man and grew up in their ways.

sentences.zh: 及長，多智謀，為群蠻所歸。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had much wisdom and stratagem and was followed by the Man tribes.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he proved clever and resourceful and came to lead the Man clans.

sentences.zh: 誕既內屬，居朗陵。

translations.literal: After Dan submitted internally, he resided at Langling.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had submitted, Huan Dan made his seat at Langling.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，王師南伐，誕請為前驅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, the royal army marched south; Dan asked to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe, when the imperial army marched south, Dan volunteered to lead the advance.

sentences.zh: 乃授使持節、南征西道大都督，討義陽，不果而還。

translations.literal: He was then granted the commissioner with staff, Grand Commander of the Western Route of the Southern Campaign, to attack Yiyang; he did not succeed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him the staff of commissioner and named him grand commander of the western wing of the southern campaign to strike Yiyang, but the effort failed and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十年，移居潁陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he moved to reside at Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he relocated his seat to Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，依例降王為公。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, according to precedent, his kingly title was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his royal title was lowered to duke, as custom required.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加征南將軍、中道大都督，征竟陵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was additionally made General Who Conquers the South and Grand Commander of the Middle Route, to campaign against Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was further named general who conquers the south and grand commander of the central route for a campaign against Jingling.

sentences.zh: 遇遷洛，師停。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, the army halted.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition was called off when the court moved the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，齊征虜將軍、直閣將軍蠻首田益宗率部曲四千餘戶內屬。

translations.literal: At that time, the Qi general who subdues captives and the direct-gate general, the Man chieftain Tian Yizong, led more than four thousand households of his following to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Man chieftain Tian Yizong, a Qi general who subdues captives and direct-gate general, brought more than four thousand households of his followers in to submit.

sentences.zh: 襄陽首雷婆思等十一人率戶千餘內自徙，求居大和川，詔給廩食。

translations.literal: Eleven leaders of Xiangyang including Lei Posi led over a thousand households to migrate inward on their own, requesting to live at Dahechuan; an edict granted them grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Posi of Xiangyang and ten others brought more than a thousand households to resettle inward, asking to live on the Dahe River; the court ordered provisions issued to them.

sentences.zh: 後開南陽，令有沔北之地，蠻人安堵，不為寇賊。

translations.literal: Later Nanyang was opened up and given the lands north of the Han; the Man people settled in peace and were no longer raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Nanyang was opened and allotted lands north of the Han, the Man settled peacefully and ceased raiding.

sentences.zh: 十八年，誕入朝，賞遇隆厚。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Dan came to court and was rewarded with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Huan Dan attended court and was honored with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰剛。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Gang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous title Gang ("resolute").

sentences.zh: 子暉，字道進，位龍驤將軍、東荊州刺史，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Hui, styled Daojin, held the rank of Flying Dragon General and Eastern Inspector of Jingzhou, and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan Hui, courtesy name Daojin, served as flying dragon general and eastern inspector of Jingzhou and succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 景明初，大陽蠻首田育丘等二萬八千戶內附，詔置四郡十八縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, the Dayang Man chieftain Tian Yuqiu and others — twenty-eight thousand households — submitted internally; an edict established four commanderies and eighteen counties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingming the Dayang Man leader Tian Yuqiu and others, some twenty-eight thousand households, submitted; the court decreed four new commanderies and eighteen counties.

sentences.zh: 暉卒。

translations.literal: Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Hui then died.

sentences.zh: 贈冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him champion general.

sentences.zh: 正光中，叔興擁所部南叛。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, Shuxing led his following in rebellion to the south.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengguang, Shuxing rebelled and fled south with his forces.

sentences.zh: 蠻首成龍強率戶數千內附，拜刺史；

translations.literal: The Man chieftain Cheng Longqiang led several thousand households to submit internally and was appointed inspector;
translations.idiomatic: The Man leader Cheng Longqiang brought several thousand households in to submit and was made an inspector;

sentences.zh: 蠻帥田牛生率戶二千內徙揚州，拜為郡守。

translations.literal: The Man commander Tian Niusheng led two thousand households to migrate inward to Yangzhou and was appointed commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Man chieftain Tian Niusheng resettled two thousand households in Yangzhou and was given a commandery governorship.

sentences.zh: 梁義州刺史邊城王文僧明、鐵騎將軍邊城太守田官德等率戶萬餘，舉州內屬。

translations.literal: Liang's Inspector of Yizhou Biancheng Wang Wensengming, Iron Cavalry General and Biancheng Prefect Tian Guande, and others led over ten thousand households, surrendering the entire province internally.
translations.idiomatic: Wensengming, the Liang inspector of Yizhou at Biancheng, and Tian Guande, iron cavalry general and prefect of Biancheng, brought more than ten thousand households and surrendered the whole province.

sentences.zh: 拜僧明平南將軍、西豫州刺史，封開封侯；

translations.literal: Wensengming was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Western Inspector of Yuzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Kaifeng;
translations.idiomatic: Wensengming was made general who pacifies the south and western inspector of Yuzhou and enfeoffed as marquis of Kaifeng;

sentences.zh: 官德龍驤將軍、義州刺史；

translations.literal: Guande was made Flying Dragon General and Inspector of Yizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Guande was named flying dragon general and inspector of Yizhou;

sentences.zh: 自余封授各有差。

translations.literal: The rest received appointments and enfeoffments according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The others received ranks and fiefs in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 僧明、官德併入朝。

translations.literal: Wensengming and Guande both came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Both Wensengming and Guande travelled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 蠻出山至邊城、建安者，八九千戶。

translations.literal: Man tribes coming out of the mountains to Biancheng and Jian'an numbered eight or nine thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Some eight or nine thousand Man households came down from the hills to Biancheng and Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 義州尋為梁將裴邃所陷。

translations.literal: Yizhou was soon seized by the Liang general Pei Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou was soon lost to the Liang general Pei Sui.

sentences.zh: 梁定州刺史田超秀亦遣使求附，請援歷年，朝廷恐輕致邊役，未之許。

translations.literal: Liang's Inspector of Dingzhou Tian Chaoxiu also sent envoys asking to submit; for years he begged for aid; the court feared lightly provoking border campaigns and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chaoxiu, the Liang inspector of Dingzhou, also sent envoys seeking to defect; he pleaded for aid year after year, but the court, wary of committing to a border war on slight grounds, held back.

sentences.zh: 會超秀死，其部曲相率內附，徙之。

translations.literal: When Chaoxiu died, his followers successively submitted internally and were relocated.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoxiu died his troops submitted en masse and were resettled.

sentences.zh: 六鎮、秦、隴所在反叛，二荊、西郢蠻大擾動，斷三鵶路，殺都督，寇盜至於襄城、汝水，百姓多被其害。

translations.literal: Where the Six Garrisons, Qin, and Long rebelled, the Man of the Two Jings and Western Ying were greatly disturbed; they cut the Sanya Road, killed the commander, and raids reached Xiangcheng and the Ru River; many common people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: As rebellion flared in the Six Garrisons and in Qin and Long, Man bands in the two Jing provinces and western Ying rose up, severed the Sanya pass, killed the area commander, and raided as far as Xiangcheng and the Ru River, bringing widespread harm to civilians.

sentences.zh: 梁遣將圍廣陵，楚城諸蠻，並為前驅。

translations.literal: Liang sent generals to besiege Guangling; the Man tribes of Chucheng all served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang generals laid siege to Guangling, and the Man of Chucheng marched in the van.

sentences.zh: 自汝水以南，恣其暴掠，連年攻討，散而復合，其暴滋甚。

translations.literal: South of the Ru River they indulged in violent plunder; year after year campaigns struck them — they scattered and reassembled, and their violence grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Ru they plundered at will. Campaign after campaign broke them apart only to see them regroup, and their depredations grew ever worse.

sentences.zh: 又有冉氏、向氏、田氏者，陬落尤盛。

translations.literal: There were also the Ran, Xiang, and Tian clans, whose settlements were especially flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ran, Xiang, and Tian clans in particular had the largest settlements.

sentences.zh: 余則大者萬家，小者千戶，更相崇樹，僭稱王侯。

translations.literal: The rest ranged from ten thousand households for the great to a thousand for the small; they mutually exalted one another and presumptuously styled themselves kings and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Others counted ten thousand households at most and a thousand at least; they raised one another up and took kingly and ducal titles without authority.

sentences.zh: 屯據三峽，斷遏水路，荊蜀行人，至有假道者。

translations.literal: They stationed themselves in the Three Gorges, blocking the water routes; travellers between Jing and Shu sometimes had to borrow passage.
translations.idiomatic: They held the Three Gorges and choked the waterways so that travellers between Jing and Shu at times had to detour through others' lands.

sentences.zh: 周文略定伊、瀍，聲教南被，諸蠻畏威，靡然向風矣。

translations.literal: Prince Wen of Zhou secured the Yi and Chan rivers; his civilizing influence spread south; the Man tribes feared his might and all turned toward him like grass in the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince Wen of Zhou had secured the Yi and Chan region, his authority reached southward and the Man clans, awed by his power, bent before him like grass in the wind.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，蔡陽蠻王魯超明內屬，授南雍州刺史，仍世襲焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, the Caiyang Man king Lu Chaoming submitted internally; he was granted the post of Inspector of Southern Yongzhou, and the title was hereditary thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong the Caiyang Man king Lu Chaoming submitted; he was made inspector of southern Yongzhou, an office his line would hold in succession.

sentences.zh: 十一年，蠻酋梅勒特來貢其方物。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Man chieftain Mei Lete came to offer tribute of local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Man leader Mei Lete presented local tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 尋而蠻帥田杜青及江、漢諸蠻擾動，大將軍楊忠擊破之。

translations.literal: Soon the Man commander Tian Duqing and the Man tribes of the Yangtze and Han were disturbed; Grand General Yang Zhong defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tian Duqing and the Man along the Yangtze and Han rose in revolt; Grand General Yang Zhong crushed them.

sentences.zh: 其後蠻帥杜青和自稱巴州刺史，入附，朝廷因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Later the Man commander Du Qinghe styled himself Inspector of Bazhou, submitted internally, and the court granted him the title he had claimed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Man chieftain Du Qinghe, who called himself inspector of Bazhou, came in to submit, and the court confirmed him under that very title.

sentences.zh: 杜青和後遂反，攻圍東梁州。

translations.literal: Du Qinghe later rebelled and besieged Eastern Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qinghe soon turned rebel and besieged eastern Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其唐州蠻田魯嘉亦叛，自號豫州伯。

translations.literal: The Tangzhou Man Tian Lujia also rebelled and styled himself Baron of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the Tangzhou Man Tian Lujia rebelled and proclaimed himself baron of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王雄、權景宣等前後討平之。

translations.literal: Wang Xiong, Quan Jingxuan, and others successively suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong, Quan Jingxuan, and others put down these rebellions one after another.

sentences.zh: 廢帝初，蠻首樊舍舉落內附，以為督淮北三州諸軍事、淮州刺史、淮安郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign, the Man chieftain Fan She led his settlement to submit internally; he was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for the Three Huai-north Provinces, Inspector of Huaizhou, and Duke of Huai'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of the deposed emperor, the Man leader Fan She brought his people in; he was made commander-in-chief of military affairs for the three Huai-north provinces, inspector of Huaizhou, and duke of Huai'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 于謹等平江陵，諸蠻騷動，詔豆盧甯、蔡祐等討破之。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin and others pacified Jiangling, the Man tribes were disturbed; an edict ordered Dou Lu Ning, Cai You, and others to campaign and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Jin took Jiangling the Man clans grew restless; the court dispatched Dou Lu Ning, Cai You, and others to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，蠻酋宜人王田興彥、北荊州刺史梅季昌等相繼款附。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong, the Man chieftain and King of Yiren Tian Xingyan, Northern Inspector of Jingzhou Mei Jichang, and others successively came in friendship and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong the Man leader Tian Xingyan, king of Yiren, and Mei Jichang, northern inspector of Jingzhou, among others, pledged allegiance in turn.

sentences.zh: 以興彥、季昌並為開府儀同三司，加季昌洛州刺史，賜爵石台縣公。

translations.literal: Xingyan and Jichang were both made Grand Master with Imperial Privilege at an Opening Office; Jichang was additionally made Inspector of Luozhou and granted the title Duke of Shitai County.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyan and Jichang were both made officials of the third rank with opening office privileges; Jichang was also named inspector of Luozhou and enfeoffed as duke of Shitai county.

sentences.zh: 其後，巴西人譙淹扇動君蠻以附梁，蠻帥向鎮侯、向白虎等應之；

translations.literal: Later, the Bazhou native Qiao Yan stirred up the Jun Man to join Liang; the Man commanders Xiang Zhenhou, Xiang Baihu, and others responded;
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiao Yan of Bazhou incited the Jun Man to side with Liang; the Man chiefs Xiang Zhenhou and Xiang Baihu answered his call;

sentences.zh: 向五子王又攻陷信州；

translations.literal: Xiang Wuzi Wang also captured Xinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Wuzi Wang likewise seized Xinzhou;

sentences.zh: 田烏度、田唐等抄斷江路；

translations.literal: Tian Wudu, Tian Tang, and others raided and cut off the Yangtze route;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wudu, Tian Tang, and others intercepted traffic on the Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 文子榮復據荊州之汶陽郡，自稱仁州刺史；

translations.literal: Wen Zirong again seized Wenyang Commandery of Jingzhou and styled himself Inspector of Renzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zirong reoccupied Wenyang commandery in Jingzhou and proclaimed himself inspector of Renzhou;

sentences.zh: 並鄰州刺史蒲微亦舉兵逆命。

translations.literal: Pu Wei, Inspector of Bingzhou, also raised troops in defiance of orders.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Wei, inspector of Bing province, also took up arms in open defiance.

sentences.zh: 詔田弘、賀若敦、潘招、李遷哲等討破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tian Hong, Heluo Dun, Pan Zhao, Li Qianzhe, and others to campaign and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Tian Hong, Heluo Dun, Pan Zhao, Li Qianzhe, and others to crush them.

sentences.zh: 周武成初，文州蠻叛，州軍討定之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wucheng of Zhou, the Wenzhou Man rebelled; the provincial army suppressed and settled it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Wucheng of Northern Zhou, the Wenzhou Man rebelled and were put down by the provincial troops.

sentences.zh: 尋而冉令賢、向五子王等又攻陷白帝，殺開府楊長華，遂相率作亂。

translations.literal: Soon Ran Lingxian, Xiang Wuzi Wang, and others again captured Baidi, killed Opening Grandee Yang Changhua, and together rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ran Lingxian, Xiang Wuzi Wang, and their allies took Baidi, killed the opening grandee Yang Changhua, and joined in open revolt.

sentences.zh: 前後遣開府元契、趙剛等總兵出討，雖頗翦其族類，而元惡未除。

translations.literal: Opening grandees Yuan Qi and Zhao Gang and others were successively dispatched to lead troops in campaign; though they cut down many of the tribes, the chief evildoers were not eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly sent opening grandees Yuan Qi and Zhao Gang at the head of armies; they pruned the rebel clans but could not root out the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，詔開府陸騰督王亮、司馬裔等討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, an edict ordered Opening Grandee Lu Teng to supervise Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others in a campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianhe the court ordered opening grandee Lu Teng, with Wang Liang and Sima Yi under his command, to lead the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 騰水陸俱進，次於湯口，先遣喻之。

translations.literal: Teng advanced by both land and water, halted at Tangkou, and first sent envoys to announce his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng pressed forward by land and river alike, making camp at Tangkou and sending envoys ahead to announce his terms.

sentences.zh: 而令賢方增浚城池，嚴設扞禦，遣其長子西黎、次子南王領其支屬，於江南險要之地，置立十城，遠結涔陽蠻為其聲援。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Lingxian was deepening and dredging city walls, setting up stern defenses, sending his eldest son Xili and second son Nanwang to lead his clansmen to ten fortified positions at strategic points south of the river, and forming distant alliances with the Cen Yang Man as his rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Lingxian was meanwhile deepening his moats, hardening his defenses, and posting his eldest son Xili and second son Nanwang with their followers at ten strong points on the river's south bank, while he called in Cen River Man allies from afar as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 令賢率其卒，固守水邏城。

translations.literal: Lingxian led his soldiers and steadfastly defended Shuoluocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxian himself held Shuoluo fortress with his main force.

sentences.zh: 騰乃總集將帥謀進趣，咸欲先取水邏，然後經略江南。

translations.literal: Teng then assembled the generals to plan the advance; all wished first to take Shuoluo and then conduct operations in the south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng gathered his commanders to plan the advance; all agreed they should seize Shuoluo first and only then subdue the south bank.

sentences.zh: 騰言於眾曰：「令賢內恃水邏金湯之險，外托涔輔車之援，兼復資糧充實，器械精新。

translations.literal: Teng said to the assembly: "Lingxian inwardly relies on the golden moat and boiling river of Shuoluo's peril; outwardly he leans on the Cen as wheel-and-axle mutual aid; moreover his stores are full and his weapons sharp and new.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng told the assembly: "Lingxian trusts in Shuoluo's impregnable walls and moat and counts on the Cen Man for mutual support; his supplies are ample and his arms fresh and keen.

sentences.zh: 以我懸軍，攻其嚴壘，脫一戰不克，更成其氣。

translations.literal: With our army cut off from base, attacking his strong fortress — if one battle fails we will only strengthen his morale.
translations.idiomatic: If we, an army far from home, hurl ourselves at his stronghold and fail in a single assault, we will only raise his spirits higher.

sentences.zh: 不如頓軍湯口，先取江南，翦其毛羽，然後游軍水邏，此制勝之計也。」

translations.literal: Better to encamp the army at Tangkou, first take the south of the river, cut off his wings, then dispatch mobile forces against Shuoluo — this is the plan for victory.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold at Tangkou, seize the south bank first and clip his wings, then send a mobile force against Shuoluo — that is the winning stratagem.

sentences.zh: 眾皆然之。

translations.literal: The assembly all assented to this.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃遣開府王亮率眾渡江，旬日攻拔其八城，凶黨奔散，獲賊帥冉承公並生口三千人，降其部眾一千戶。

translations.literal: He then sent Opening Grandee Wang Liang to lead the army across the river; within ten days eight cities were taken; the wicked scattered and fled; the rebel commander Ran Chenggong was captured along with three thousand captives, and one thousand households of his followers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent opening grandee Wang Liang across the river; in ten days eight fortresses fell, the rebels scattered, and Ran Chenggong was taken along with three thousand captives while a thousand households surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂簡募驍勇，數道分攻水邏。

translations.literal: He then selected and recruited the bold and brave, and divided them into several routes to attack Shuoluo separately.
translations.idiomatic: Next he picked the best fighters and sent them in several columns against Shuoluo.

sentences.zh: 路經石壁城，險峻，四面壁立，故以名焉。

translations.literal: The route passed through Shibi Fortress, steep and precipitous, with walls standing on all four sides — hence its name.
translations.idiomatic: The road ran through Shibi ("Stone Wall") fortress, sheer on every side — which is how it got its name.

sentences.zh: 唯有一小路，緣梯而上，蠻蜒以為峭絕，非兵眾所行。

translations.literal: There was only one small path, ascending by ladder; the Man tribes considered it sharply sheer and impassable for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Only one narrow track climbed up by ladder; the Man thought it too steep for any army to pass.

sentences.zh: 騰被甲先登，眾軍繼進，備經危阻，累日乃得舊路。

translations.literal: Teng donned armor and climbed first; the army followed; after much peril and obstruction, many days passed before they regained the old road.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng armored himself and led the climb; the troops followed through repeated hazards until, after many days, they won through to the main road.

sentences.zh: 且騰先任隆州總管，雅知其路蠻帥冉伯犁、冉安西與令賢有隙。

translations.literal: Moreover, Teng had previously served as Inspector-General of Longzhou and well knew that the route's Man commanders Ran Boli and Ran Anxi had enmity with Lingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng had once been inspector-general of Longzhou and knew that the local Man chiefs Ran Boli and Ran Anxi were at odds with Lingxian.

sentences.zh: 騰乃招誘伯犁等，結為父子，又多遺錢帛。

translations.literal: Teng then recruited and enticed Boli and the others, forming with them a bond of adoptive father and sons, and sent many gifts of money and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He wooed Boli and the others, swearing bonds of adoptive kinship and showering them with coin and silk.

sentences.zh: 伯犁等悅，遂為鄉導。

translations.literal: Boli and the others were pleased and then served as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Boli and his men became guides through the hills.

sentences.zh: 水邏側又有石勝城者，亦是險要，令賢使其兄龍真據之。

translations.literal: Beside Shuoluo there was also Shisheng Fortress, likewise strategic; Lingxian had his elder brother Longzhen hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Near Shuoluo stood Shisheng fortress, another strong point held by Lingxian's elder brother Longzhen.

sentences.zh: 勝又密告龍真雲，若平水邏，使其代令賢處之。

translations.literal: Teng again secretly told Longzhen, saying that if Shuoluo were pacified, he would be allowed to take Lingxian's place in holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng secretly promised Longzhen that if Shuoluo fell, he would receive Lingxian's seat.

sentences.zh: 龍真大悅，遣其子詣騰。

translations.literal: Longzhen was greatly pleased and sent his son to Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed, Longzhen sent his son to Lu Teng.

sentences.zh: 乃厚加禮接，賜以金帛。

translations.literal: He was treated with generous courtesy and granted gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng received the son with full honors and gave him gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 蠻貪利既深，仍請立效，乃謂騰曰：「欲翻所據城，恐人力寡少。」

translations.literal: The Man tribes, their greed for profit now deep, still asked to prove their merit and said to Teng: "We wish to turn over the fortress we hold, but fear our numbers are too few.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for reward, they offered to defect, telling Lu Teng: "We mean to turn over our fortress, but we fear our numbers are too small.

sentences.zh: 騰許以三百兵助之。

translations.literal: Teng promised three hundred soldiers to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng pledged three hundred troops to aid them.

sentences.zh: 既而遣二千人，銜枚夜進，龍真力不能禦，遂平石勝城。

translations.literal: Then he sent two thousand men, advancing at night with gags in their mouths; Longzhen could not resist and Shisheng Fortress was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he sent two thousand men advancing silently by night; Longzhen could not hold them off and Shisheng fortress was taken.

sentences.zh: 晨至水邏，蠻眾大潰，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: At dawn they reached Shuoluo; the Man forces collapsed in great rout; more than ten thousand heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn they were at Shuoluo; the Man army broke and fled; more than ten thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 令賢遁走，追而獲之。

translations.literal: Lingxian fled in escape; he was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxian fled but was run down and captured.

sentences.zh: 司馬裔又別下其二十餘城，獲蠻帥冉三公等。

translations.literal: Sima Yi separately reduced more than twenty of their cities and captured the Man commander Ran San'gong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi meanwhile reduced more than twenty strongholds and seized the Man chiefs Ran San'gong and others.

sentences.zh: 騰乃積其骸骨于水邏城側為京觀，後蠻蜒望見輒大哭，自此狼戾之心輟矣。

translations.literal: Teng then piled their bones beside Shuoluo into a victory mound; afterward when the Man tribes saw it they would burst into loud weeping, and from then on their ferocious hearts ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng piled the slain into a victory mound beside Shuoluo; when the Man later saw it they wailed, and their savage will was broken from that day on.

sentences.zh: 時向五子王據石墨城，令其子寶勝據雙城。

translations.literal: At that time Xiang Wuzi Wang held Shimo Fortress and had his son Baosheng hold Shuangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xiang Wuzi Wang held Shimo fortress while his son Baosheng garrisoned Shuangcheng.

sentences.zh: 水邏平後，頻遺喻之，而五子王猶不從命。

translations.literal: After Shuoluo was pacified, he repeatedly sent envoys to instruct him, yet Wuzi Wang still would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuoluo fell, Lu Teng sent envoys again and again to summon him, but Wuzi Wang still refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 騰又遣王亮屯牢坪，司馬裔屯雙城以圖之。

translations.literal: Teng again sent Wang Liang to garrison Laoping and Sima Yi to garrison Shuangcheng in order to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Teng then posted Wang Liang at Laoping and Sima Yi at Shuangcheng to hem them in.

sentences.zh: 騰慮雙城孤峭，攻未可拔，賊若委城遁散，又難追討。

translations.literal: Teng feared that Shuangcheng was isolated and steep, that an assault might not succeed in taking it, and that if the rebels abandoned the city and scattered in flight, they would again be hard to pursue and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Teng worried that Shuangcheng, perched alone on steep ground, might not fall to assault—and that if the rebels slipped away and dispersed, they would be nearly impossible to run down.

sentences.zh: 乃令諸軍周回立柵，遏其走路，賊乃大駭。

translations.literal: He then ordered the armies to encircle and erect palisades, blocking their routes of escape, and the rebels were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He had his forces ring the area with palisades and cut off every escape route; the rebels were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 於是縱兵擊破之，禽五子王於石墨，獲寶勝於雙城，悉斬諸向首領，生禽萬餘口。

translations.literal: Thereupon he unleashed his troops and defeated them, capturing Wuzi Wang at Shimo and seizing Baosheng at Shuangcheng; he beheaded all the Xiang chieftains and took more than ten thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: He then unleashed his troops and broke them: Wuzi Wang was taken at Shimo, Baosheng at Shuangcheng, every Xiang chieftain was executed, and more than ten thousand captives were seized alive.

sentences.zh: 信州舊居白帝，騰更于劉備故宮城南，八陳之北，臨江岸築城，移置信州。

translations.literal: Xinzhou had formerly been located at Baidi; Teng rebuilt a city south of Liu Bei's old palace, north of the Eight Formations, on the riverbank, and moved Xinzhou there.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou had long sat at Baidi; Teng built a new city south of Liu Bei's old palace, north of the Eight Formations, on the riverbank, and moved the prefectural seat there.

sentences.zh: 又以巫縣、信陵、秭歸併築城置防，以為襟帶焉。

translations.literal: He also jointly built fortified cities and set up defenses at Wu County, Xinling, and Zigui, making them a strategic belt.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise fortified Wu, Xinling, and Zigui into a defensive chain that guarded the approaches.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，蠻渠冉祖裛、冉龍驤又反，詔大將軍趙訚討平之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe the Man chieftains Ran Zuyi and Ran Longxiang rebelled again; an edict ordered Grand General Zhao Yin to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe the Man chiefs Ran Zuyi and Ran Longxiang rose again; the court ordered Grand General Zhao Yin to put them down.

sentences.zh: 自此群蠻懼息，不復為寇。

translations.literal: From then on the Man tribes feared and subsided, no longer raiding.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Man tribes were cowed into quiet and no longer raided.

sentences.zh: 獠者，蓋南蠻之別種，自漢中達於邛、笮，川洞這間，所在皆有。

translations.literal: The Liao are a separate branch of the southern Man, reaching from Hanzhong to Qiong and Zuo, and between river valleys and caves they are found everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao were a distinct branch of the southern Man peoples, ranging from Hanzhong to Qiong and Zuo; wherever river valleys and mountain hollows ran, they were there.

sentences.zh: 種類甚多，散居山谷，略無氏族之別。

translations.literal: Their kinds are very numerous; they live scattered in mountain valleys and largely have no distinction of clans.
translations.idiomatic: Their clans were many, scattered through mountain valleys, with scarcely any organized lineage structure.

sentences.zh: 又無名字，所生男女，唯以長幼次第呼之。

translations.literal: They also have no personal names; the boys and girls they bear are called only by order of seniority.
translations.idiomatic: They used no personal names at all: children were addressed simply by birth order.

sentences.zh: 其丈夫稱阿謨、阿段，婦人阿夷、阿等之類，皆語之次第稱謂也。

translations.literal: Their men are called Amo, Aduan, and the like; women Ayi, Adeng, and so on—all are terms of address by order in their language.
translations.idiomatic: Men went by forms such as Amo and Aduan, women by Ayi and Adeng—terms that marked rank in the family rather than true names.

sentences.zh: 依樹積木，以居其上，名曰幹闌，幹闌大小，隨其家口之數。

translations.literal: They pile wood against trees and live above it; this is called ganlan; the size of a ganlan follows the number of mouths in the household.
translations.idiomatic: They built stilt houses of timber against trees—ganlan, they called them—sized to fit however many people lived under one roof.

sentences.zh: 往往推一長者為王，亦不能遠相統攝。

translations.literal: They often choose one elder as king, yet he cannot govern them from afar.
translations.idiomatic: They would often elevate an elder as king, but his authority did not reach far beyond his own valley.

sentences.zh: 父死則子繼，若中國之貴族也。

translations.literal: When the father dies the son succeeds, like the nobility of the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: When a father died his son succeeded him, much like a hereditary noble house in the heartland.

sentences.zh: 獠王各有鼓角一雙，使其子弟自吹擊之。

translations.literal: Each Liao king has one pair of drums and horns, which his sons and younger kinsmen blow and strike themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Every Liao king kept a drum and horn, which his sons and kinsmen sounded themselves.

sentences.zh: 好相殺害，多死，不敢遠行。

translations.literal: They are fond of killing one another; deaths are many, and they dare not travel far.
translations.idiomatic: They feuded constantly; bloodshed was common, and few ventured far from home.

sentences.zh: 能臥水底持刀刺魚，其口嚼食並鼻飲。

translations.literal: They can lie underwater and stab fish with knives; they chew food with their mouths and also drink through their noses.
translations.idiomatic: They could lie on the riverbed and spear fish with a knife; they ate by chewing and drank by drawing liquid through the nose.

sentences.zh: 死者，豎棺而埋之。

translations.literal: When someone dies, they bury him in an upright coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were buried in coffins set upright in the ground.

sentences.zh: 性同禽獸，至於忿怒，父子不相避，唯手有兵刃者先殺之。

translations.literal: Their nature is like that of birds and beasts; when anger rises, father and son do not avoid one another—whoever has a weapon in hand kills first.
translations.idiomatic: Their tempers were bestial: in a rage, father and son would strike without hesitation, and whoever held a blade struck first.

sentences.zh: 若殺其父，走避外，求得一狗以謝，不復嫌恨。

translations.literal: If one kills his father, he flees and stays away, obtains a dog to offer in apology, and resentment does not return.
translations.idiomatic: If a man killed his father, he fled into exile, then returned a dog as blood payment—and the feud was considered closed.

sentences.zh: 若報怨相攻擊，必殺而食之；

translations.literal: When settling grudges and attacking one another, they must kill and eat the foe;
translations.idiomatic: In blood feuds they killed their enemies and ate the flesh;

sentences.zh: 平常劫掠，賣取豬狗而已。

translations.literal: in ordinary plunder they sell captives only for pigs and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: in ordinary raids they sold captives for no more than pigs or dogs.

sentences.zh: 親戚比鄰，指授相賣。

translations.literal: Kinsmen and neighbors point out victims and sell one another.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and neighbors would identify victims and trade them among themselves.

sentences.zh: 被賣者號哭不服，逃竄避之，乃將買人指捕，逐若亡叛，獲便縛之。

translations.literal: Those sold wail and refuse submission, flee and hide; then the buyer is led to seize them, pursued as if they were deserters, and once caught they are bound.
translations.idiomatic: The victim would wail and bolt; the buyer, guided to the spot, hunted him down like a fugitive rebel and bound him on capture.

sentences.zh: 但經被縛者，即服為賤隸，不敢稱良矣。

translations.literal: Whoever has once been bound submits and becomes a base slave, no longer daring to call himself free.
translations.idiomatic: Once bound, a man accepted servile status and never again claimed to be free.

sentences.zh: 亡失兒女，一哭便止，不復追思。

translations.literal: When sons and daughters are lost, they weep once and stop, no longer brooding over it.
translations.idiomatic: If a child was lost, they wept once and moved on, without lingering grief.

sentences.zh: 唯執楯持矛，不識弓矢。

translations.literal: They only grasp shields and hold spears; they do not know bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They fought with shield and spear alone and knew nothing of bow and arrow.

sentences.zh: 用竹為簧，群聚鼓之，以為音節。

translations.literal: They use bamboo as reeds, gather and beat them, and take this as rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: They made bamboo reeds and beat them in groups for music and dance.

sentences.zh: 能為細布，色至鮮淨。

translations.literal: They can weave fine cloth, its colors extremely bright and clean.
translations.idiomatic: They wove fine cloth of striking, vivid color.

sentences.zh: 大狗一頭，賣一生口。

translations.literal: One large dog buys one living captive.
translations.idiomatic: A full-grown dog was the price of one captive.

sentences.zh: 其俗畏鬼神，尤尚淫祀。

translations.literal: Their custom fears ghosts and spirits and especially honors excessive sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: They feared ghosts and spirits and were devoted above all to lavish, excessive rites.

sentences.zh: 所殺之人美鬢髯者，乃剝其面皮，籠之於竹，及燥，號之曰鬼，鼓舞祀之，以求福利。

translations.literal: Of those they kill, if one has handsome whiskers and beard, they flay his face skin, cage it in bamboo, and when dry call it a ghost; they dance and drum to sacrifice to it, seeking blessing.
translations.idiomatic: When they killed a man with a fine beard, they flayed his face, stretched the skin on a bamboo frame, and when it dried called it a ghost—then danced and drummed before it to win favor from the spirits.

sentences.zh: 至有賣其昆季妻孥盡者，乃自賣以供祭焉。

translations.literal: Some even sell off all their brothers' wives and children, then sell themselves to supply the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Some sold every brother's wife and child, then sold themselves into bondage to pay for the rites.

sentences.zh: 鑄銅為器，大口寬腹，名曰銅爨，既薄且輕，易於熟食。

translations.literal: They cast bronze into vessels—wide mouth, broad belly—called tongcuan; thin and light, they cook food quickly.
translations.idiomatic: They cast bronze cauldrons with wide mouths and bellies—tongcuan, they called them—thin, light, and quick to boil a meal.

sentences.zh: 建國中，李勢在蜀，諸獠始出巴西、渠川、廣漢、陽安、資中，攻破郡國，為益州大患。

translations.literal: During Jianguo, when Li Shi held Shu, the Liao first came out from Baxi, Quchuan, Guanghan, Yang'an, and Zizhong, stormed commanderies and kingdoms, and became a great calamity to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianguo, while Li Shi ruled Shu, the Liao poured out of Baxi, Quchuan, Guanghan, Yang'an, and Zizhong, overran the districts, and became Yizhou's gravest scourge.

sentences.zh: 勢內外受敵，所以亡也。

translations.literal: Shi was attacked within and without; this is why he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi was beset from within and without—and that is why his realm fell.

sentences.zh: 自桓溫破蜀之後，力不能制。

translations.literal: After Huan Wen broke Shu, the court lacked the strength to control them.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen conquered Shu, the court no longer had the strength to hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 又蜀人東流，山險之地多空，獠遂挾山傍穀。

translations.literal: Moreover, as Shu people flowed eastward, the steep mountain lands stood largely empty, and the Liao then clung to mountains and hugged valleys.
translations.idiomatic: As Sichuan's Han population drifted eastward, the mountain fastnesses emptied, and the Liao settled along ridges and ravines.

sentences.zh: 與夏人參居者，頗輸租賦；

translations.literal: Those who lived intermixed with the Xia people paid a fair amount of taxes and levies;
translations.idiomatic: Where they lived among Han settlers they paid a measure of tax and tribute;

sentences.zh: 在深山者，仍不為編戶。

translations.literal: those in deep mountains still were not entered in the household registers.
translations.idiomatic: those in the deep hills remained outside the tax rolls altogether.

sentences.zh: 梁、益二州歲伐獠，以裨潤公私，頗藉為利。

translations.literal: Liang and Yi provinces annually campaigned against the Liao to supplement and enrich public and private coffers, relying on this for considerable profit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Yi provinces raided the Liao every year, padding both public and private purses—a trade many found profitable.

sentences.zh: 正始中，夏侯道遷舉漢中內附，宣武遣尚書邢巒為梁、益二州刺史以鎮之，近夏人者安堵樂業，在山谷者不敢為寇。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi, Xiahou Daqian raised Hanzhong and submitted internally; Emperor Xuanwu sent Minister of the Interior Xing Luan as Inspector of Liang and Yi to garrison them; those near the Xia people settled in peace and took joy in their work, while those in mountain valleys did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, Xiahou Daqian brought Hanzhong over to the north; Emperor Xuanwu sent Xing Luan to govern Liang and Yi. Liao near Han settlements lived quietly and worked the land; those in the valleys no longer dared raid.

sentences.zh: 後以羊祉為梁州，傅豎眼為益州。

translations.literal: Later Yang Zhi was made Inspector of Liangzhou and Fu Shuyan Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Zhi was appointed to Liangzhou and Fu Shuyan to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祉性酷虐，不得物情。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was cruel and tyrannical; he did not win the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi was brutal and won no one's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 梁輔國將軍范季旭與獠王趙清荊率眾屯孝子穀，祉遣統軍魏胡擊走之。

translations.literal: Liang's General Who Supports the State Fan Jixu and the Liao king Zhao Qingjing led their masses to camp at Xiaozi Valley; Zhi sent Commander Wei Hu to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jixu, general who supports the state of Liang, and the Liao king Zhao Qingjing massed at Xiaozi Valley; Yang Zhi sent Wei Hu to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 後梁甯朔將軍姜白復擁夷獠入屯南城，梁州人王法慶與之通謀，眾屯於固門川。

translations.literal: Later Liang's General Who Pacifies the North Jiang Bai again gathered barbarian Liao and entered to camp at Nancheng; Wang Faqing of Liangzhou conspired with him, and their host camped at Gumen River.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiang Bai, Liang's pacifier of the north, rallied Liao tribes and seized Nancheng; Wang Faqing of Liangzhou joined the plot, and their forces gathered on the Gumen River.

sentences.zh: 祉遣征虜將軍討破之。

translations.literal: Zhi sent a General Who Punishes Barbarians to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi sent a punitive general who broke them.

sentences.zh: 豎眼施恩布信，大得獠和。

translations.literal: Shuyan bestowed favor and spread good faith, greatly winning the Liao's accord.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan ruled with generosity and kept his word, and the Liao came willingly to his side.

sentences.zh: 後以元法僧代傅豎眼為益州，法僧在任貪殘，獠遂反叛，勾引梁兵，圍逼晉壽。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Faseng replaced Fu Shuyan as Inspector of Yizhou; Faseng in office was greedy and cruel, and the Liao then rebelled, drawing in Liang troops and besieging Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Faseng succeeded Fu Shuyan in Yizhou; greedy and savage in office, he drove the Liao into revolt. They called in Liang armies and pressed Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂之，以豎眼先得物情，復令乘傳往撫。

translations.literal: The court was troubled by this; because Shuyan had earlier won the people's hearts, he was again ordered to ride post-haste to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed; because Fu Shuyan had once won the people's trust, he was sent post-haste to restore order.

sentences.zh: 獠聞豎眼至，莫不欣然，拜迎道路，於是而定。

translations.literal: When the Liao heard Shuyan had arrived, none failed to rejoice; they bowed and welcomed him along the roads, and order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Fu Shuyan was coming, the Liao turned out joyfully along the roads to greet him, and the region settled.

sentences.zh: 及元桓、元子真相繼為梁州，並無德績，諸獠苦之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Huan and Yuan Zizhen succeeded one another as Inspector of Liangzhou, neither had virtue or achievement, and the Liao suffered under them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huan and Yuan Zizhen followed one after another in Liangzhou, neither with merit or mercy, and the Liao groaned under their rule.

sentences.zh: 其後，朝廷以梁、益二州控攝險遠，乃立巴州以統諸獠。

translations.literal: Afterward the court, because Liang and Yi provinces controlled steep and distant lands, established Bazhou to govern the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: The court then created Bazhou to govern the Liao, for Liang and Yi alone could not hold such rugged, distant country.

sentences.zh: 後以巴酋嚴始欣為刺史。

translations.literal: Later the Ba chieftain Yan Shixin was made Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Ba chieftain Yan Shixin was appointed inspector.

sentences.zh: 又立隆城鎮，所綰獠二十萬戶。

translations.literal: Longcheng garrison was also established, administering two hundred thousand Liao households.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison was set at Longcheng to oversee two hundred thousand Liao households.

sentences.zh: 彼謂北獠，歲輸租布，又與外人交通貿易。

translations.literal: These were called the northern Liao; each year they paid cloth as tax and also traded with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: These northern Liao paid an annual cloth levy and traded freely with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 巴州生獠，並皆不順，其諸頭王，每于時節謁見刺史而已。

translations.literal: The raw Liao of Bazhou were all unsubmissive; their various head kings merely paid seasonal visits to the inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The wild Liao of Bazhou obeyed no one; their head kings came only at festival times to pay courtesy calls on the inspector.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，諸獠以始欣貪暴，相率反叛，攻圍巴州。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaochang the Liao, because Shixin was greedy and violent, rebelled together and besieged Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang the Liao rose together against Yan Shixin's greed and cruelty and laid siege to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 山南行台魏子建勉喻，即時散罷。

translations.literal: Wei Zijian of the Shannan Executive Board urged them earnestly, and they immediately dispersed and quit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zijian of the Shannan executive board talked them down, and they broke up at once.

sentences.zh: 自是獠諸頭王，相率詣行台者相繼，子建厚勞賚之。

translations.literal: From then on the Liao head kings came in succession to the executive board; Zijian richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Liao head kings came one after another to the executive board, and Wei Zijian treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 始欣見中國多事，又失彼心，慮獲罪譴，時梁南梁州刺史陰子春扇惑邊陲，始欣謀將南叛。

translations.literal: Shixin saw the Central States beset by many troubles and had also lost their hearts; fearing punishment, and with Yin Zichun, Inspector of Southern Liangzhou of Liang, then stirring the borderlands, Shixin plotted to defect south.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shixin saw the empire in turmoil and knew he had lost the Liao's trust; fearing reprisal, and with Yin Zichun of Liang stirring the frontier, he plotted to go over to the south.

sentences.zh: 始欣族子愷時為隆城鎮將，密知之，嚴設邏候，遂禽梁使人，並封始欣詔書、鐵券、刀劍、衣冠之屬，表送行台。

translations.literal: Shixin's clansman Kai, then commandant of Longcheng garrison, learned of it in secret, set strict border watches, seized Liang's envoys, and sealed up Shixin's edicts, iron certificates, swords, robes, and the like, reporting all to the executive board.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Yan Kai, garrison commandant at Longcheng, learned of the plot, tightened the border posts, seized Liang's envoys, and sent the court a sealed packet of Shixin's edicts, iron bonds, arms, and regalia.

sentences.zh: 子建乃啟以豎眼久病，其子敬紹納始欣重賂，使得還州。

translations.literal: Zijian then memorialized that Shuyan had long been ill and that his son Jingshao had accepted heavy bribes from Shixin, allowing him to return to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zijian reported that Fu Shuyan, long ill, had let his son Jingshao take Yan Shixin's heavy bribes and restore him to office.

sentences.zh: 始欣乃起眾攻愷，屠滅之，據城南叛。

translations.literal: Shixin then raised his host, attacked Kai, slaughtered and destroyed him, seized the city, and rebelled south.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shixin raised his forces, attacked Yan Kai, wiped him out, seized the city, and declared for the south.

sentences.zh: 梁將蕭玩，率眾援接。

translations.literal: The Liang general Xiao Wan led troops to support and link up with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Xiao Wan marched to his aid.

sentences.zh: 時梁、益二州並遣將討之，攻陷巴州，執始欣，遂大破玩軍。

translations.literal: At the time Liang and Yi provinces both sent generals to punish them, stormed Bazhou, seized Shixin, and then thoroughly defeated Wan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Yi both sent generals against them, retook Bazhou, captured Yan Shixin, and routed Xiao Wan's army.

sentences.zh: 及斬玩，以傅曇表為刺史。

translations.literal: When Wan was beheaded, Fu Tanbiao was made Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Wan was executed, and Fu Tanbiao was appointed inspector.

sentences.zh: 後元羅在梁州，為所陷，自此遂絕。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Luo was in Liangzhou and was trapped by them; from then on contact was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Luo, holding Liangzhou, was undone by them, and from that point the region was lost.

sentences.zh: 及周文平梁、益之後，令在所撫慰，其與華人雜居者，亦頗從賦役。

translations.literal: After Yuwen Tai pacified Liang and Yi, he ordered local officials to soothe and comfort them; those who lived mixed with the Chinese also largely submitted to taxes and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Tai pacified Liang and Yi, local officials were told to win them over; Liao living among Han settlers largely accepted tax and corvée duty.

sentences.zh: 然天性暴亂，旋致擾動。

translations.literal: Yet by nature they are violent and unruly, and soon disturbances arose again.
translations.idiomatic: But they were violent by nature, and trouble flared again before long.

sentences.zh: 每歲命隨近州鎮，出兵討之，獲其生口，以充賤隸，謂之為壓獠焉。

translations.literal: Each year nearby provinces and garrisons were ordered to campaign against them; captives taken alive were used as base slaves—this was called pressing the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Every year nearby prefectures and garrisons were sent against them; captives were taken as bond servants in what was called 'pressing the Liao.'

sentences.zh: 後有商旅往來者，亦資以為貨，公卿達於人庶之家，有獠口者多矣。

translations.literal: Later when merchants traveled back and forth, they also traded in them as goods; from ministers and grandees down to common households, many had Liao captives.
translations.idiomatic: Later merchants traded in them too; from high officials to humble homes, Liao bondsmen were common.

sentences.zh: 恭帝三年，陵州木籠獠反，詔開府陸騰討破之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong, the Mulung Liao of Lingzhou rebelled; an edict ordered Chief Commandant Lu Teng to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Gong the Mulung Liao of Lingzhou rebelled; Lu Teng was ordered out and broke them.

sentences.zh: 周保定二年，鐵山獠又反，抄斷江路，陸騰又攻拔其三城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding of Zhou the Tieshan Liao rebelled again, cutting and blocking the river routes; Lu Teng again attacked and took three of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's second year of Baoding the Tieshan Liao rose again and cut the river routes; Lu Teng stormed three of their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，梁州恆棱獠叛，總管長史趙文表討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe the Hengling Liao of Liangzhou rebelled; Chief Administrator Zhao Wenbiao was sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe the Hengling Liao of Liangzhou rebelled, and Chief Administrator Zhao Wenbiao was dispatched against them.

sentences.zh: 軍次巴州，文表欲率眾徑進。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Bazhou, Wenbiao wished to lead the host straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Bazhou, and Zhao Wenbiao meant to march straight in.

sentences.zh: 軍吏等曰：「此獠旅拒日久，部眾甚強，討之者四面攻之，以分其勢。

translations.literal: The staff officers said: "These Liao have resisted as a host for a long time; their followers are very strong. Those who suppress them should attack from four sides to divide their strength.
translations.idiomatic: His officers said, "These Liao have held out a long time and their numbers are strong. The usual way is to attack from four sides and split their force.

sentences.zh: 今若大軍直進，不遣奇兵，恐亻並力於我，未可制勝。」

translations.literal: If the main army now advances straight in without sending surprise troops, I fear they will combine their strength against us and victory may not be assured.
translations.idiomatic: If the main force pushes straight ahead without a flanking column, they may mass against us and we may not win.

sentences.zh: 文表曰：「往者既不能制之，今須別為進趣。

translations.literal: Wenbiao said: "In the past we could not control them; now we must take a different line of advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao replied, "We failed to control them before; this time we must advance differently.

sentences.zh: 若四面遣兵，則獠降走路絕，理當相率以死拒戰；

translations.literal: If we send troops on four sides, the Liao's routes of surrender and flight will be cut off, and they will naturally band together to fight to the death;
translations.idiomatic: Send troops on every side and we cut off every path of flight—they will band together and fight to the death;

sentences.zh: 如從一道，則吾得示威恩，分遣人以理曉諭，為惡者討之，歸善者撫之，善惡既分，易為經略。

translations.literal: if we go by one route, then we can display both sternness and kindness, send men separately to explain reason, punish the wicked and soothe the good; once good and evil are divided, control is easy.
translations.idiomatic: march by a single route and we can show both force and mercy, send envoys to reason with them, punish the guilty and reassure the willing—once the good and bad are sorted, the rest is manageable.

sentences.zh: 事有變通，奈何欲遵前轍也？」

translations.literal: Affairs allow flexibility—why insist on following the old track?
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances call for flexibility—why cling to the old plan?

sentences.zh: 文表遂以此意，遍令軍中。

translations.literal: Wenbiao then spread this intent throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao then made this plan known throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 時有從軍熟獠，多與恆棱親識，即以實報之。

translations.literal: At the time there were seasoned Liao in the army who knew many Hengling people personally; they reported the truth to them.
translations.idiomatic: Some Liao soldiers in his ranks knew the Hengling people well and told them exactly what was planned.

sentences.zh: 恆棱獠相與聚議，猶豫之間，文表軍已至其界。

translations.literal: The Hengling Liao gathered to consult together; while they hesitated, Wenbiao's army had already reached their border.
translations.idiomatic: The Hengling Liao met to debate their response—but while they wavered, Zhao Wenbiao's army was already at their border.

sentences.zh: 獠中先有二路，一路稍平，一路極險。

translations.literal: Among the Liao there were first two routes: one somewhat level, one extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Two routes led into Liao country: one fairly level, the other brutally steep.

sentences.zh: 俄有生獠酋帥數人來見文表曰：「我恐官軍不識山川，請為鄉導。」

translations.literal: Soon several raw Liao chieftains came to see Wenbiao and said: "I fear the official army does not know the mountains and rivers; please let us serve as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Soon several wild Liao chiefs came to Zhao Wenbiao and said, "We fear your troops do not know the country—let us guide you.

sentences.zh: 文表謂之曰：「此路寬平，不須導引，卿但先去，好慰喻子弟也。」

translations.literal: Wenbiao said to them: "This route is broad and level; it needs no guide. You need only go ahead first and comfort and instruct your followers well.
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "This road is wide and easy—you need no guide. Go on ahead and reassure your people.

sentences.zh: 乃遣之。

translations.literal: He then sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: And he sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 文表謂其眾曰：「向者獠帥，謂吾從寬路而行，必當設伏險要。

translations.literal: Wenbiao said to his host: "The Liao chiefs just now assumed we would take the broad route and will surely set ambushes at perilous points.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao told his men, "Those chiefs think we will take the easy road and will surely lay ambushes at the passes.

sentences.zh: 若從險路，出其不慮，獠眾自離散矣。」

translations.literal: If we take the perilous route and catch them unawares, the Liao masses will scatter of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Take the hard road and catch them off guard, and their forces will fall apart on their own.

sentences.zh: 於是勒兵從險道進，其有不通之處，即平之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drove his troops forward by the perilous path; wherever it was impassable, he cleared it.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops up the hard trail, cutting through wherever the way was blocked.

sentences.zh: 乘高而望，果見其伏兵。

translations.literal: Climbing high to look, he indeed saw their ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: From a height he looked down and saw the ambush exactly where he had expected.

sentences.zh: 獠既失計，爭攜妻子，退保險要。

translations.literal: The Liao, their plan having failed, all grabbed wives and children and withdrew to hold perilous strongpoints.
translations.idiomatic: Outmaneuvered, the Liao grabbed their families and fell back to the mountain redoubts.

sentences.zh: 文表頓軍大蓬山下，示禍福，遂相率來降。

translations.literal: Wenbiao halted his army below Mount Dapeng, showed them fortune and disaster, and they then came to surrender in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao camped below Mount Dapeng, showed them the choice between ruin and mercy, and they surrendered in waves.

sentences.zh: 文表皆撫慰之，仍征其租稅，無敢動者。

translations.literal: Wenbiao soothed and comforted them all, then levied their taxes and rents; none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He reassured them all, collected their taxes, and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 後除文表為蓬州刺史，又大得人和。

translations.literal: Later Wenbiao was appointed Inspector of Pengzhou and again greatly won men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao was later made inspector of Pengzhou and again won broad loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建德初，李暉為蓬、梁州總管，諸獠亦望風從附。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiande, Li Hui was Chief Administrator of Peng and Liang provinces; the Liao also, seeing the wind, followed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jian' de, Li Hui became chief administrator of Peng and Liang, and the Liao submitted at the first sign of his authority.

sentences.zh: 然其種滋蔓，保據嚴壑，依山走險，若履平地，雖屢加兵，弗可窮討。

translations.literal: Yet their kind spread and proliferated, holding fast to steep ravines; relying on mountains they ran perilous paths as if treading level ground. Though troops were repeatedly sent against them, they could not be thoroughly pursued and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their clans continued to spread, clinging to steep ravines and moving along mountain defiles as easily as walking flat ground. Repeated military campaigns could not root them out.

sentences.zh: 性又無知，殆同禽獸，諸夷之中，最難以道招懷者也。

translations.literal: Their nature was also ignorant, almost like birds and beasts; among all the frontier peoples, they were the hardest to win over by moral persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: Their temperament was crude, scarcely above that of animals; among all the frontier peoples they were the least responsive to conciliation and civilized rule.

sentences.zh: 林邑，其先所出，事具《南史》。

translations.literal: Linyi — the origins of its founders are fully recorded in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The origins of Linyi are related in full in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 其國延袤數千里，土多香木、金寶，物產大抵與交趾同。

translations.literal: Its state extended several thousand li; the soil had much fragrant timber and gold and jewels; its products were in general the same as Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom stretched for thousands of li, rich in fragrant timber and precious metals; its products were much the same as those of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 以磚為城，蜃灰塗之，東向戶。

translations.literal: They made their walls of brick, plastered them with clam-shell lime, and their doors faced east.
translations.idiomatic: Their cities were built of brick coated with shell lime, with doorways facing east.

sentences.zh: 尊官有二，其一曰西那婆帝，其二曰薩婆地歌。

translations.literal: There were two exalted offices: the first called Xina-podi, the second Sapodi-ge.
translations.idiomatic: Two supreme offices existed: one called Xina-podi, the other Sapodi-ge.

sentences.zh: 其屬官三等，其一曰倫多姓，次歌倫致帝，次乙地伽蘭。

translations.literal: Their subordinate officials were of three ranks: the first called Lunduoxing, next Gelun-zhi-di, next Yidi-jialan.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials fell into three ranks: Lunduoxing, Gelun-zhi-di, and Yidi-jialan.

sentences.zh: 外官分為二百餘部，其長官曰弗羅，次曰可輪，如牧宰之差也。

translations.literal: Outer officials were divided into more than two hundred departments; their chief was called Fuluo, the next rank Kelun, like the difference between pastoral administrators and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Local administration was divided into more than two hundred districts, headed by officers called Fuluo, with subordinates called Kelun—the equivalent of prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 王戴金花冠，形如章甫，衣朝霞布，珠璣纓絡，足躡革履，時服錦袍。

translations.literal: The king wore a golden-flower crown shaped like a zhangfu cap, dressed in morning-glow cloth, with pearl and gem tassels and chains, and on his feet leather shoes; at times he wore brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a golden flower crown shaped like a formal cap, robes of dawn-colored cloth adorned with pearls and gems, and leather shoes, sometimes switching to brocade gowns.

sentences.zh: 良家子侍衛者二百許人，皆執金裝。

translations.literal: About two hundred scions of good families served as guards, all bearing gilded arms.
translations.idiomatic: Some two hundred youths from respectable families served as guards, all armed with gilded weapons.

sentences.zh: 兵有弓、箭、刀、槊。

translations.literal: Their soldiers had bows, arrows, knives, and spears.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops carried bows, arrows, swords, and long spears.

sentences.zh: 以為竹為弩，傅毒於矢。

translations.literal: They made crossbows of bamboo and smeared poison on the arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They fashioned bamboo crossbows and tipped their arrows with poison.

sentences.zh: 樂有琴、笛、琵琶、五弦，頗與中國同。

translations.literal: In music they had zither, flute, pipa, and five-stringed lute — much the same as in China.
translations.idiomatic: Their music featured zithers, flutes, pipa, and five-stringed lutes, much like those of China.

sentences.zh: 每擊鼓以警眾，吹蠡以即戎。

translations.literal: Whenever they beat drums to alert the masses, they blew conch shells to take up arms.
translations.idiomatic: Drums summoned the people; conch shells signaled mobilization for war.

sentences.zh: 其人深目高鼻，發拳色黑。

translations.literal: Their people had deep-set eyes and high noses; their hair was curly and black in color.
translations.idiomatic: The people had deep-set eyes, prominent noses, and tight curly black hair.

sentences.zh: 俗皆徒跣，以幅巾纏身，冬月衣袍。

translations.literal: Customarily all went barefoot, wrapping their bodies in cloth head-bands; in winter months they wore robes.
translations.idiomatic: They went barefoot by custom, wrapping themselves in cloth bands, and wore robes in winter.

sentences.zh: 婦人椎髻。

translations.literal: Women wore chignons.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore their hair in topknot chignons.

sentences.zh: 施椰葉席。

translations.literal: They spread coconut-leaf mats.
translations.idiomatic: Coconut-leaf mats served as bedding.

sentences.zh: 每有婚媾，令媒者齎金銀釧、酒二壺、魚數頭至女家，於是擇日，夫家會親賓，歌舞相對，女家請一婆羅門送女至男家，婿盥手，因牽女授之。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a marriage, they had the matchmaker bring gold and silver bracelets, two jars of wine, and several fish to the bride's house; then a day was chosen, the groom's family gathered kin and guests with song and dance facing each other, the bride's family asked a Brahmin to escort the girl to the groom's house, the groom washed his hands, and thus led the girl and handed her over.
translations.idiomatic: For weddings a matchmaker brought gold and silver bracelets, two jars of wine, and several fish to the bride's home. On the chosen day the groom's family assembled relatives and guests for singing and dancing; a Brahmin escorted the bride to the groom's house, where the groom washed his hands and took her hand in marriage.

sentences.zh: 王死，七日而葬；

translations.literal: When the king died, burial came after seven days;
translations.idiomatic: When the king died, he was buried after seven days;

sentences.zh: 有官者，三日；

translations.literal: for those with office, three days;
translations.idiomatic: officials after three days;

sentences.zh: 庶人，一日。

translations.literal: commoners, one day.
translations.idiomatic: commoners after one day.

sentences.zh: 皆以函盛屍，鼓舞導從，輿至水次，積薪焚之。

translations.literal: All placed the corpse in a coffin, with drum-and-dance escorts leading the way, carried it in a bier to the water's edge, heaped firewood, and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: The body was placed in a coffin and borne with singing and dancing to the water's edge, where it was burned on a pyre.

sentences.zh: 收其餘骨，王則內金罌中，沉之於海；

translations.literal: They gathered the remaining bones; for the king they placed them in a golden urn and sank it in the sea;
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bones were collected; for the king they were placed in a golden urn and cast into the sea;

sentences.zh: 有官者，以銅罌，沉之海口；

translations.literal: for those with office, a bronze urn, sunk at the mouth of the sea;
translations.idiomatic: for officials, in a bronze urn sunk at the seashore;

sentences.zh: 庶人以瓦，送之于江。

translations.literal: commoners used pottery and sent them down the river.
translations.idiomatic: for commoners, in earthenware vessels sent down the river.

sentences.zh: 男女皆截發，哭至水次，盡哀而止，歸則不哭。

translations.literal: Men and women all cut their hair, wept until they reached the water's edge, exhausted their grief and stopped; once home they wept no more.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women cut their hair and mourned at the water's edge until grief was spent; once they returned home, weeping ceased.

sentences.zh: 每七日，燃香散花，復哭盡哀而止，百日、三年皆如之。

translations.literal: Every seven days they burned incense and scattered flowers, again weeping until grief was exhausted and stopping; at one hundred days and three years it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Every seven days they burned incense and scattered flowers and mourned again until grief was spent—the same at the hundred-day mark and at three years.

sentences.zh: 人皆奉佛，文字同於天竺。

translations.literal: All the people revered Buddhism; their writing was the same as in Tianzhu (India).
translations.idiomatic: All practiced Buddhism, and their script was the same as that of India.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝既平陳，乃遣使獻方物，後朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen of Sui had pacified Chen, they sent envoys presenting local products; afterward tribute missions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Sui conquered Chen, Linyi sent envoys bearing tribute, but the missions soon lapsed.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，群臣言林邑多奇寶者。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was at peace; ministers spoke of how Linyi had many rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire at peace, court officials spoke of the rare treasures said to abound in Linyi.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，上遣大將軍劉方為驩州道行軍總管，率欽州刺史甯長真、驩州刺史李暈、開府秦雄步騎萬餘，及犯罪者數千人擊之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Renshou era, the emperor dispatched General Liu Fang as Commander of the Campaign Route of Huan Province, leading Inspector of Qinzhou Ning Changzhen, Inspector of Huanzhou Li Hun, and Kaifu Qin Xiong with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry, along with several thousand convicts, to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era the emperor sent General Liu Fang as campaign commander on the Huan route, leading Qinzhou inspector Ning Changzhen, Huanzhou inspector Li Hun, and Kaifu Qin Xiong with over ten thousand foot and horse soldiers plus several thousand convicts to attack Linyi.

sentences.zh: 其王梵志乘巨象而戰，方軍不利。

translations.literal: Its king Fan Zhi rode a huge elephant into battle; Fang's army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: King Fan Zhi fought mounted on a great elephant, and Liu Fang's army was hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 方乃多掘小坑，草覆其上，因以兵挑之。

translations.literal: Fang then dug many small pits and covered them with grass, then used troops to provoke them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang had many small pits dug and covered with grass, then sent men to taunt the enemy.

sentences.zh: 方與戰偽北，梵志逐之，其象陷，軍遂亂，方大破之，遂棄城走。

translations.literal: Fang fought and feigned retreat; Fan Zhi pursued, his elephant sank in, the army then fell into disorder, and Fang routed them utterly; they abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang feigned retreat in battle; Fan Zhi gave chase, his elephant became mired, and his army broke in confusion. Liu Fang won a great victory, and the Linyi forces abandoned their city and fled.

sentences.zh: 入其都，獲其廟主十八枚，皆鑄金為之，盡其國有十八世。

translations.literal: Entering their capital, they captured eighteen temple images, all cast in gold, representing the full eighteen generations of their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital they seized eighteen gilded temple images representing all eighteen reigns of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 方班師，梵志復其故地，遣使謝罪，於是朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: Fang withdrew his army; Fan Zhi recovered his former territory and sent envoys to apologize; from then on tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang withdrew, but Fan Zhi regained his former lands and sent envoys to apologize; tribute missions thereafter continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 赤土國，扶南之別種也。

translations.literal: The state of Chi Tu was a separate branch of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Chi Tu (Red Earth) was an offshoot of Funan.

sentences.zh: 在南海中，水行百餘日而達。

translations.literal: It lay in the southern sea; by water one reached it after more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: It lay in the southern seas, more than a hundred days' voyage by ship.

sentences.zh: 所都土色多赤，因以為號。

translations.literal: At its capital the soil was mostly red; hence they took it as their name.
translations.idiomatic: The soil around the capital was predominantly red, which gave the kingdom its name.

sentences.zh: 東波羅刺國，西婆羅娑國，南訶羅旦國，北拒大海，地方數千里。

translations.literal: To the east was Boluoci state, to the west Poluosuo state, to the south Heluodan state, and to the north it faced the great sea; its territory was several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Boluoci to the east, Poluosuo to the west, and Heluodan to the south, with the open sea to the north; its domain covered several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 其王姓瞿曇氏，多利富多塞，不知有國近遠。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Gautama; his name was Taripura; he had no knowledge of how near or far other states were.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Gautama clan and was named Taripura; he had little sense of how near or far other kingdoms lay.

sentences.zh: 稱其父釋王位，出家為道，傳位於利富多塞，在位十六年矣。

translations.literal: He said his father had abdicated the throne, left home to follow the Way, and passed the throne to Taripura, who had already reigned sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He said his father had renounced the throne to become a monk and had passed rule to Taripura, who had already reigned sixteen years.

sentences.zh: 有三妻，並鄰國女也。

translations.literal: He had three wives, all daughters of neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: He had three wives, all princesses from neighboring kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 居僧祗城，有門三重，相去各百許步。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Sengqi city, which had three gates, each about a hundred paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Sengqi city, which had three gates spaced about a hundred paces apart.

sentences.zh: 每門圖畫菩薩飛仙之象，懸金花鈴眊，婦人數十人，或奏樂，或捧金花。

translations.literal: At each gate were painted images of bodhisattvas and flying immortals; golden-flower bells and banners were hung; several dozen women either played music or held golden flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate was painted with bodhisattvas and flying immortals and hung with golden bells and banners; dozens of women played music or bore golden flowers.

sentences.zh: 又飾四婦人，容飾如佛塔邊金剛力士之狀，夾門而立，門外者持兵仗，門內者執白拂。

translations.literal: Four women were also adorned, their appearance like the vajra guardian figures beside a Buddhist pagoda, standing flanking the gate; those outside held weapons, those inside held white fly-whisks.
translations.idiomatic: Four women were dressed like the vajra guardians flanking a pagoda, standing on either side of the gate; attendants outside bore weapons, those inside carried white fly-whisks.

sentences.zh: 夾道垂素網，綴花。

translations.literal: Along the road hung white nets strung with flowers.
translations.idiomatic: White nets hung along the road, decorated with flowers.

sentences.zh: 王宮諸屋，悉是重閣北戶。

translations.literal: All the buildings of the royal palace were multi-storied pavilions with doors facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The palace buildings were all multi-storied halls with north-facing doors.

sentences.zh: 北面而坐三重之榻，衣朝霞布，冠金花冠，垂雜寶纓絡，四女子立侍左右，兵衛百餘人。

translations.literal: Facing north he sat on a triple-tiered couch, dressed in morning-glow cloth, wearing a golden-flower crown with assorted jewel tassels and chains; four women stood attending left and right, and more than a hundred soldiers guarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He sat facing north on a triple-tiered throne, wearing dawn-colored robes and a golden flower crown hung with jeweled tassels; four women stood at his side and more than a hundred guards attended him.

sentences.zh: 王榻後作一木龕，以金銀五香木雜鈿之，龕後懸一金光焰；

translations.literal: Behind the king's couch stood a wooden shrine inlaid with gold, silver, and assorted fragrant woods; behind the shrine hung a golden flame-disk;
translations.idiomatic: Behind the throne stood a wooden shrine inlaid with gold, silver, and fragrant woods; behind it hung a golden flame emblem;

sentences.zh: 夾榻又樹二金鏡，鏡前並陳金甕，甕前各有金香爐；

translations.literal: flanking the couch stood two golden mirrors; before the mirrors were set out golden urns, and before each urn was a golden incense burner;
translations.idiomatic: flanking the throne stood two golden mirrors, with golden urns before them and a golden incense burner before each urn;

sentences.zh: 當前置一金伏牛，前樹一寶蓋，左右皆有寶扇。

translations.literal: directly in front stood a golden recumbent ox; before it rose a jeweled canopy, and on left and right were jeweled fans.
translations.idiomatic: directly in front stood a golden recumbent ox, with a jeweled canopy before it and jeweled fans on either side.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門等數百人，東西重行，相向而坐。

translations.literal: Several hundred Brahmins and others sat in double rows east and west, facing one another.
