translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Brahmins sat in facing rows to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 其官：薩陀加邏一人，陀拏達叉一人，迦利密迦三人，共掌政事；

translations.literal: Their offices: one Satagaluo, one Tanadacha, and three Kalimika jointly managed state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The chief offices were Satagaluo, Tanadacha, and three Kalimika, who jointly managed government affairs;

sentences.zh: 俱羅末帝一人，掌刑法。

translations.literal: one Juluomodi, who managed penal law.
translations.idiomatic: and Juluomodi, who oversaw criminal law.

sentences.zh: 每城置那邪迦一人，缽帝十人。

translations.literal: In each city one Nayaka and ten Bodi were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Each city had one Nayaka and ten Bodi officials.

sentences.zh: 其俗，皆穿耳翦發，無跪拜之禮，以香油塗身。

translations.literal: Their custom: all pierced their ears and cut their hair; there was no ritual of kneeling and bowing; they smeared fragrant oil on their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Customarily they pierced their ears and cut their hair, observed no kneeling or bowing ritual, and anointed their bodies with fragrant oil.

sentences.zh: 其俗敬佛，尤重婆羅門。

translations.literal: Their custom revered Buddhism and especially honored Brahmins.
translations.idiomatic: They revered Buddhism and held Brahmins in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 婦人作髻于項後，男女通以朝霞朝雲雜色布為衣。

translations.literal: Women made their chignons at the nape; men and women alike commonly wore dawn-glow, dawn-cloud, and assorted-colored cloth as clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore chignons at the nape of the neck; both sexes commonly dressed in dawn-colored and multicolored cloth.

sentences.zh: 豪富之室，恣意華靡，唯金鎖非王賜不得服用。

translations.literal: In wealthy households they indulged in lavish ornament; only golden chains could not be worn unless bestowed by the king.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households dressed as lavishly as they pleased, but golden chains could be worn only when granted by the king.

sentences.zh: 每婚嫁，擇吉日，女家先期五日，作樂飲酒，父執女手以授婿，七日乃配。

translations.literal: For each marriage they chose an auspicious day; the bride's family five days beforehand made music and drank wine; the father took the girl's hand and gave her to the groom; only after seven days were they formally paired.
translations.idiomatic: For weddings an auspicious day was chosen; five days beforehand the bride's family feasted with music and wine, and the father placed his daughter's hand in the groom's; the couple was formally united after seven days.

sentences.zh: 既娶，即分財別居，唯少子與父居。

translations.literal: Once married, they immediately divided property and lived apart; only the youngest son dwelt with the father.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage sons divided the household property and lived separately; only the youngest remained with his father.

sentences.zh: 父母兄弟死，則剔發素服，就水上構竹木為棚，棚內積薪，以屍置上，燒香建幡，吹蠡擊鼓以送，火焚薪，遂落于水。

translations.literal: When parents or brothers died, they shaved their heads and wore plain mourning dress; by the water they built a bamboo-and-wood shed, heaped firewood inside, placed the corpse on top, burned incense and raised banners, blew conch shells and beat drums to send them off; when the fire burned the wood, it then fell into the water.
translations.idiomatic: When parents or siblings died, mourners shaved their heads and wore plain white dress. By the water they built a bamboo scaffold, piled firewood on it, and placed the body atop; incense was burned and banners raised while conch shells and drums sounded. When the pyre burned through, the remains fell into the water.

sentences.zh: 貴賤皆同、唯國王燒訖收灰，貯以金瓶，藏於廟屋。

translations.literal: Nobles and commoners were the same; only the king, after the burning was finished, gathered the ashes, stored them in a golden flask, and kept them in a temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and commoners followed the same rite; only the king, after cremation, collected the ashes in a golden flask and stored them in a temple.

sentences.zh: 冬夏常溫，雨多霽少，種植無時。

translations.literal: Winter and summer were constantly warm; rain was frequent and clear weather rare; planting had no fixed season.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was warm year-round, with more rain than sunshine and no fixed planting season.

sentences.zh: 特宜稻、穄、白豆、黑麻，自餘物產，多同於交趾。

translations.literal: It was especially suited to rice, millet, white beans, and black hemp; the rest of its products were largely the same as Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Rice, millet, white beans, and black hemp grew especially well; other products were much like those of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 以甘蔗作酒，雜以紫瓜根，酒色黃赤，味亦香美。

translations.literal: They made wine from sugarcane mixed with purple gourd root; the wine's color was yellow-red, and the flavor was also fragrant and fine.
translations.idiomatic: They brewed wine from sugarcane mixed with purple gourd root; it was yellow-red in color and fragrant on the palate.

sentences.zh: 亦以椰漿為酒。

translations.literal: They also made wine from coconut milk.
translations.idiomatic: Coconut sap was also fermented into wine.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝嗣位，募能通絕域者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang of Sui succeeded to the throne, he recruited men able to reach distant lands beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang of Sui came to the throne, he sought men capable of reaching distant lands beyond the empire.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，屯田主事常駿、虞部主事王君政等請使赤土。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, Chang Jun, chief clerk of the military colonies, Wang Junzheng, chief clerk of the parks bureau, and others requested to be sent as envoys to Chi Tu.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 3, Chang Jun of the military colonies bureau and Wang Junzheng of the parks bureau petitioned to lead an embassy to Chi Tu.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遣齎物五千段以賜赤土王。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and dispatched them bearing five thousand rolls of goods to bestow on the king of Chi Tu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and sent them with five thousand rolls of silk and goods as gifts for the king of Chi Tu.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，駿等自南海郡乘舟，晝夜二旬，每日遇便風。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, Jun and the others embarked from Nanhai commandery; day and night for twenty days they sailed, each day meeting favorable winds.
translations.idiomatic: That October Chang Jun and his party sailed from Nanhai commandery; for twenty days and nights they enjoyed favorable winds each day.

sentences.zh: 至焦石山而過，東南詣陵伽缽拔多洲，西與林邑相對，上有神祠焉。

translations.literal: They passed Jiaoshi Mountain and proceeded southeast to Lingjiaboduozhou isle, which faced Linyi to the west; upon it stood a spirit shrine.
translations.idiomatic: They passed Jiaoshi Mountain and sailed southeast to Lingjiaboduozhou isle, facing Linyi to the west, where a spirit shrine stood.

sentences.zh: 又南行，至師子石。

translations.literal: They sailed south again and reached Shizi Rock.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing south, they reached Lion Rock.

sentences.zh: 自是島嶼連接。

translations.literal: From there islands linked one to another.
translations.idiomatic: From there onward islands lay in an unbroken chain.

sentences.zh: 又行二三日，西望見狼牙須國之山，於是南達雞籠島，至於赤土之界。

translations.literal: After two or three more days' sailing, looking west they saw the mountains of Langyaxu state; then proceeding south they reached Jilong isle and arrived at the border of Chi Tu.
translations.idiomatic: After two or three more days they sighted to the west the mountains of Langyaxu; sailing south they reached Jilong isle and entered Chi Tu territory.

sentences.zh: 其王遣婆羅門鳩摩羅，以舶三百艘來迎，吹蠡擊鼓樂隋使，進金鎖以纜船。

translations.literal: Its king sent the Brahmin Jiumoluo with three hundred ships to welcome them, blowing conch shells and beating drums to entertain the Sui envoys, presenting golden chains to moor the ships.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent the Brahmin Jiumoluo with three hundred vessels to welcome them, greeting the Sui envoys with conch shells and drums and presenting golden chains to moor their ships.

sentences.zh: 月餘，至其都。

translations.literal: After more than a month they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 王遣其子那邪迦請與駿等禮見。

translations.literal: The king sent his son Nayaka to invite Jun and the others to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent his son Nayaka to invite Chang Jun and his party to an audience.

sentences.zh: 先遣人送金盤貯香花並鏡鑷，金合二枚貯香油，金瓶二枚貯香水，白疊布四條，以擬供使者盥洗。

translations.literal: First they sent men bearing a golden tray holding fragrant flowers together with mirror and tweezers, two golden boxes holding fragrant oil, two golden flasks holding scented water, and four lengths of white cotton cloth, intended to supply the envoys for washing.
translations.idiomatic: They first sent a golden tray of flowers and incense with mirror and tweezers, two golden boxes of fragrant oil, two golden flasks of scented water, and four lengths of white cotton cloth for the envoys' ablutions.

sentences.zh: 其日未時，那邪迦又將象二頭，持孔雀獸以迎使人，並致金盤、金花，以藉詔函，男女百人奏蠡鼓，婆羅門二人導路。

translations.literal: That day at the wei hour Nayaka again led two elephants and carried peacock beasts to welcome the envoys, also presenting golden trays and golden flowers to cushion the imperial letter-case; a hundred men and women played conch drums, and two Brahmins led the way.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon Nayaka came again with two elephants and peacock-feather standards to welcome the envoys, presenting golden trays and flowers to cushion the imperial letter-case; a hundred attendants played conch drums while two Brahmins led the procession.

sentences.zh: 至王宮，駿等奉詔書上閣，王以下皆坐，宣詔訖，引駿等坐，奏天竺樂，事畢，駿等還館。

translations.literal: Reaching the royal palace, Jun and the others presented the imperial edict and ascended the hall; the king and all below sat; when the edict had been read they led Jun and the others to seats, Indian music was performed, and when the affair was finished Jun and the others returned to their lodging.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace Chang Jun and his party presented the imperial edict in the upper hall; the king and his court were seated, and after the edict was read they were given seats while Indian music was played. When the ceremony ended they returned to their quarters.

sentences.zh: 又遣婆羅門就館送食，以草葉為盤，其大方丈。

translations.literal: They again sent Brahmins to the lodging to bring food, using leaves as plates about a zhang square.
translations.idiomatic: Brahmins were sent to their quarters with food served on leaf platters each about a square zhang in size.

sentences.zh: 因謂駿曰：「今是大國臣，非復赤土國矣。」

translations.literal: He then said to Jun: "You are now subjects of the great state; you are no longer of Chi Tu.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chang Jun, "You are now subjects of the great empire, no longer merely of Chi Tu.

sentences.zh: 後數日，請駿等入宴，儀衛導從如初見之禮。

translations.literal: Several days later he invited Jun and the others to a banquet; guards and escorts conducted them with the same ceremony as at the first audience.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later they were invited to a banquet, escorted with the same ceremonial guard as at their first audience.

sentences.zh: 王前設兩床，床上並設草葉盤，方一丈五尺，上有黃、白、紫、赤四色之餅，牛、羊、魚、鱉、豬、蝳蝐之肉百餘品。

translations.literal: Before the king two couches were set; on each couch were leaf platters a zhang and five chi square, bearing yellow, white, purple, and red cakes, and more than a hundred kinds of beef, mutton, fish, turtle, pork, and oyster meat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the king stood two couches, each with leaf platters a zhang and a half square holding yellow, white, purple, and red cakes and more than a hundred dishes of beef, mutton, fish, turtle, pork, and shellfish.

sentences.zh: 延駿升床，從者于地席，各以金鍾置酒，女樂迭奏，禮遺甚厚。

translations.literal: They invited Jun to ascend the couch; his followers sat on ground mats; each had a golden goblet with wine set before him; female musicians played in succession; the courtesy and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jun was seated on the couch while his attendants sat on mats below, each with a golden cup of wine; female musicians performed in turn, and the hospitality was lavish.

sentences.zh: 尋遣那邪迦隨貢方物，並獻金芙蓉冠、龍腦香，以鑄金為多羅葉，隱起成文以為表，金函封之，令婆羅門以香花奏蠡鼓而送之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they sent Nayaka to accompany tribute goods, also presenting a golden lotus crown and camphor; they cast gold into bodhi-leaf form with raised inscriptions as a memorial, sealed it in a golden case, and had Brahmins send them off with fragrant flowers while playing conch drums.
translations.idiomatic: Nayaka was soon dispatched with tribute goods, including a golden lotus crown and camphor; a gold bodhi leaf cast with raised inscription served as their memorial, sealed in a golden case and sent off with Brahmins playing conch drums amid flowers and incense.

sentences.zh: 既入海，見綠魚群飛水上。

translations.literal: Once they had entered the sea, they saw green fish flying in groups above the water.
translations.idiomatic: Once at sea they saw shoals of green fish skimming the surface.

sentences.zh: 浮海十餘日，至林邑東南，並山而行。

translations.literal: They floated on the sea for more than ten days, reached the southeast of Linyi, and sailed along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days at sea they reached southeastern Linyi and sailed along the coast.

sentences.zh: 其海水色黃氣腥，舟行一日不絕，雲是大魚糞也。

translations.literal: The seawater there was yellow in color and foul-smelling; sailing for a full day one could not pass through it; they said it was the droppings of great fish.
translations.idiomatic: The water there was yellow and foul-smelling; a full day's sailing could not carry them clear of it—they were told it was the excrement of great fish.

sentences.zh: 循海北岸，達於交趾。

translations.literal: Following the northern shore of the sea, they reached Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: They followed the northern coast until they reached Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 駿以六年春與那邪迦于弘農謁帝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year Jun together with Nayaka had an audience with the emperor at Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 6 Chang Jun presented Nayaka to the emperor at Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，授駿等執戟都尉，那邪迦等官賞各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed Jun and the others Commandants Bearing Halberds; Nayaka and the others received official rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and made Chang Jun and his party Commandants Bearing Halberds; Nayaka and his companions received titles and rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 真臘國，在林邑西南，本扶南之屬國也，去日南郡舟行六十日而至。

translations.literal: The state of Zhenla lay southwest of Linyi; it was originally a subject state of Funan; from Rinan commandery one reached it by ship in sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Zhenla lay southwest of Linyi. Originally a vassal of Funan, it was sixty days' voyage by ship from Rinan commandery.

sentences.zh: 南接車渠國，西有硃江國。

translations.literal: To the south it adjoined Chequ state; to the west was Zhujiang state.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Chequ to the south and Zhujiang to the west.

sentences.zh: 其王姓刹利氏，名質多斯那。

translations.literal: Its king bore the surname Kshatriya; his name was Citrasena.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Kshatriya clan and was named Citrasena.

sentences.zh: 自其祖漸已強盛，至質多斯那隧兼扶南而有之。

translations.literal: From his ancestors they had gradually grown strong; by the time of Citrasena they had seized Funan and possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: His dynasty had grown steadily stronger since his forebears' time; under Citrasena it conquered Funan and absorbed its territory.

sentences.zh: 死，子伊奢那先代立。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Ishanavarman succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Ishanavarman succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 居伊奢那城，郭下二萬餘家。

translations.literal: They dwelt in Ishana city; outside the walls were more than twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was Ishana city, with more than twenty thousand households in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 城中有一大堂，是其王聽政所。

translations.literal: Within the city was one great hall, where the king held court and heard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The city had a great hall that served as the king's council chamber.

sentences.zh: 總大城三十所，城有數千家，各有部帥，官名與林邑同。

translations.literal: In all there were thirty great cities; each city had several thousand households; each had its own regional commander; official titles were the same as in Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom comprised thirty major cities of several thousand households each, each with its own regional commander; official titles matched those of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 其王三日一聽朝，坐五香七寶床，上施寶帳，以文木為竿，象牙金鈿為壁，狀如小屋，懸金光焰，有同於赤土。

translations.literal: The king held court every three days; he sat on a bed of five fragrant woods and seven treasures, with a jeweled canopy above; using patterned wood for poles and ivory with gold inlay for walls, shaped like a small house; a golden flame-disk was hung — the same as in Chi Tu.
translations.idiomatic: The king held court every third day, seated on a couch of fragrant woods and seven treasures beneath a jeweled canopy, with a pavilion of carved wood poles and ivory walls inlaid with gold, like a small house, and a golden flame emblem suspended — much as in Chi Tu.

sentences.zh: 前有金香，命二人侍側。

translations.literal: Before him stood a golden incense burner; he ordered two men to attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: A golden incense burner stood before him, attended by two servants at his side.

sentences.zh: 王著朝霞古貝，瞞絡腰腹，下垂至脛，頭載金寶花冠，被真珠纓絡，足履革屣，耳懸金鐺。

translations.literal: The king wore morning-glow cloth and ancient cotton, wrapping his loins and waist, hanging down to the shins; on his head he bore a golden jeweled flower crown, draped with pearl tassels and chains; on his feet leather sandals; from his ears hung golden bells.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore dawn-colored robes and cotton cloth wrapped about his waist to the shins, a golden jeweled crown, pearl necklaces, leather sandals, and golden ear pendants.

sentences.zh: 常服白疊，以象牙為屩。

translations.literal: For ordinary dress he wore white cotton cloth and used ivory for shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In everyday dress he wore white cotton and ivory sandals.

sentences.zh: 若露發，則不加纓絡。

translations.literal: If his hair was uncovered, he did not wear tassels and chains.
translations.idiomatic: When his hair was uncovered, he wore no pearl necklaces.

sentences.zh: 臣下服制，大抵相類。

translations.literal: The dress regulations of ministers and subordinates were in general similar.
translations.idiomatic: The dress of his officials was generally similar.

sentences.zh: 有五大臣，一曰孤落支，二曰相高憑，三曰婆何多陵，四曰舍摩陵，五曰髯羅婁，及諸小臣。

translations.literal: There were five great ministers: the first called Guluozhi, the second Xianggaoping, the third Poheduoling, the fourth Shemolin, the fifth Ranluolou, and various lesser ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Five great ministers — Guluozhi, Xianggaoping, Poheduoling, Shemolin, and Ranluolou — headed the court, with various lesser officials below them.

sentences.zh: 朝于王者，輒於階下三稽首，王呼上階，則跪，以兩手抱膊，繞王環坐。

translations.literal: When attending upon the king, they always performed three prostrations at the foot of the steps; when the king summoned them up the steps they knelt, clasping their arms with both hands, and sat in a circle around the king.
translations.idiomatic: Officials attending the king prostrated three times at the foot of the steps; when summoned up they knelt with arms folded and sat in a circle around him.

sentences.zh: 議政事訖，跪伏而去。

translations.literal: When deliberation on state affairs was finished, they knelt prostrate and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When business was concluded they prostrated themselves and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 階庭門閣，侍衛有千餘人，被甲持仗。

translations.literal: On the steps, courts, gates, and pavilions, guards numbered more than a thousand, wearing armor and bearing weapons.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand armored guards with weapons stood watch on the steps, courtyards, gates, and halls.

sentences.zh: 其國與參半、硃江二國和親，數與林邑、陀桓二國戰爭。

translations.literal: This state was allied by marriage with the two states of Canban and Zhujiang, and frequently fought wars with the two states of Linyi and Tuohuan.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom was allied by marriage with Canban and Zhujiang but frequently at war with Linyi and Tuohuan.

sentences.zh: 其人行止，皆持甲仗，若有征伐，因而用之。

translations.literal: In going about, all the people bore armor and weapons; if there was a campaign, they used them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The people went about armed at all times, ready for use whenever war was needed.

sentences.zh: 其俗，非王正妻子，不得為嗣。

translations.literal: By their custom, only the king's legitimate wife's children could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: By custom only children born to the king's lawful wife could inherit the throne.

sentences.zh: 王初立日，所有兄弟，並刑殘之，或去一指，或劓其鼻，別處供給，不得仕進。

translations.literal: On the day the king first ascended, all his brothers were mutilated by punishment — some had a finger removed, some had their noses cut off — housed separately and supplied, and could not enter office or advance.
translations.idiomatic: When a king acceded, all his brothers were mutilated — a finger cut off or nose severed — housed apart on an allowance and barred from office.

sentences.zh: 人形小而色黑，婦人亦有白者。

translations.literal: The people's bodies were small and black in color; among women there were also fair-skinned ones.
translations.idiomatic: The people were short and dark-skinned, though some women were fair.

sentences.zh: 悉拳發垂耳，性氣捷勁。

translations.literal: All had curly hair and pendant ears; their nature and temperament were quick and vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: They wore their hair curly and ears pendant; by nature they were quick and vigorous.

sentences.zh: 居處器物，頗類赤土。

translations.literal: Their dwellings, utensils, and implements were much like those of Chi Tu.
translations.idiomatic: Their dwellings and furnishings closely resembled those of Chi Tu.

sentences.zh: 以右手為淨，左手為穢。

translations.literal: They took the right hand as pure and the left hand as defiled.
translations.idiomatic: The right hand was considered pure, the left defiled.

sentences.zh: 每旦澡洗，以楊枝淨齒，讀誦經咒，又澡灑乃食。

translations.literal: Each morning they bathed and washed, used willow twigs to clean their teeth, read and recited sutras and spells, bathed and sprinkled themselves again, and then ate.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning they bathed, cleaned their teeth with willow twigs, recited scriptures and spells, washed again, and then ate.

sentences.zh: 食罷還用楊枝淨齒，又讀經咒。

translations.literal: When eating was finished they again used willow twigs to clean their teeth and again read sutras and spells.
translations.idiomatic: After meals they again cleaned their teeth with willow twigs and recited scriptures.

sentences.zh: 飲食多蘇酪、沙糖、秔粟、米餅。

translations.literal: In food and drink they mostly had ghee, granulated sugar, polished millet, and rice cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Their diet featured ghee, granulated sugar, polished millet, and rice cakes.

sentences.zh: 欲食之時，先取雜肉羹與餅相和，手擩而食。

translations.literal: When about to eat, they first took assorted meat broth and mixed it with cakes, kneading it by hand to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Before eating they mixed assorted meat broth with rice cakes and ate it kneaded by hand.

sentences.zh: 娶妻者唯送女人女，擇日遣媒人迎婦。

translations.literal: For taking a wife they only sent the girl; a day was chosen and a matchmaker was dispatched to fetch the bride.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage required only that the bride's family send the girl; on the chosen day a matchmaker came to fetch her.

sentences.zh: 男女二家，各八日不出，晝夜燃燈不息。

translations.literal: The bride's and groom's two families each stayed indoors for eight days without going out; lamps burned day and night without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Both families remained indoors for eight days, lamps burning day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 男婚禮畢，即與父母分財別居。

translations.literal: When the man's marriage rites were finished, he immediately divided property with his parents and lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: Once the wedding was complete the man divided the family property and set up his own household.

sentences.zh: 父母死，小兒未婚者，以餘財與之。

translations.literal: When parents died, unmarried younger sons were given the remaining property.
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, unmarried sons received the remaining estate.

sentences.zh: 若婚畢，財物入官。

translations.literal: If marriage was completed, property and goods went to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If they had already married, their inheritance passed to the state.

sentences.zh: 喪葬，兒女皆七日不食，剔發而喪，僧尼、道士、親故皆來聚會，音樂送之。

translations.literal: At funeral and burial, sons and daughters all fasted for seven days without eating, shaved their heads in mourning; monks, nuns, Daoist priests, and kin all came to gather; music accompanied the send-off.
translations.idiomatic: At funerals sons and daughters fasted seven days and shaved their heads in mourning; monks, nuns, Brahmin priests, and kin gathered, with music to send off the dead.

sentences.zh: 以五香木燒屍，收灰，以金銀瓶盛，送大水之內；

translations.literal: They burned the corpse with five fragrant woods, gathered the ashes, placed them in gold or silver flasks, and sent them into great waters;
translations.idiomatic: The body was burned with fragrant wood; the ashes were collected in gold or silver vessels and released into great waters;

sentences.zh: 貧者或用瓦，而以五彩色畫之。

translations.literal: The poor might use pottery, painting it in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Poorer families used painted pottery vessels instead.

sentences.zh: 亦有不焚，送屍山中，任野獸食者。

translations.literal: There were also those who did not burn but sent the corpse into the mountains, leaving it for wild beasts to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Some did not cremate but left bodies in the mountains for wild beasts.

sentences.zh: 其國北多山阜，南有水澤。

translations.literal: In their state the north had many hills and mounds; the south had water marshes.
translations.idiomatic: The northern part of the kingdom was mountainous; the south was wetland.

sentences.zh: 地氣尤熱，無霜雪，饒瘴癘毒蜇。

translations.literal: The land's qi was especially hot; there was no frost or snow; miasma, pestilence, and venomous stings were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was extremely hot, with no frost or snow and abundant miasma and venomous creatures.

sentences.zh: 宜粱、稻，少黍、粟。

translations.literal: Suitable crops were sorghum and rice; millet and grain were few.
translations.idiomatic: Sorghum and rice grew well; millet and grain were scarce.

sentences.zh: 果菜與日南、九真相類。

translations.literal: Fruits and vegetables were much like those of Rinan and Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits and vegetables resembled those of Rinan and Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 異者，有婆羅那娑樹，無花，葉似柿，實似冬瓜；

translations.literal: Among unusual ones was the polona tree, without flowers; leaves like persimmon, fruit like winter melon;
translations.idiomatic: Distinctive trees included the polona, flowerless, with persimmon-like leaves and winter-melon-like fruit;

sentences.zh: 庵羅樹，花、葉似棗，實似李；

translations.literal: The amra tree — flowers and leaves like jujube, fruit like plum;
translations.idiomatic: the amra, with jujube-like flowers and leaves and plum-like fruit;

sentences.zh: 毗野樹，花似木瓜，葉似杏，實似楮；

translations.literal: The biye tree — flowers like quince, leaves like apricot, fruit like paper-mulberry;
translations.idiomatic: the biye, with quince-like flowers, apricot-like leaves, and paper-mulberry-like fruit;

sentences.zh: 婆田羅樹，花、葉、實並似棗而小異；

translations.literal: The botianluo tree — flowers, leaves, and fruit all like jujube but slightly different;
translations.idiomatic: the botianluo, resembling the jujube in flower, leaf, and fruit but slightly distinct;

sentences.zh: 歌畢佗樹，花似林檎，葉似榆而厚大，實似李，其大如升。

translations.literal: The gebita tree — flowers like crab apple, leaves like elm but thick and large, fruit like plum, as large as a sheng measure.
translations.idiomatic: the gebita, with crab-apple flowers, thick elm-like leaves, and plum-sized fruit as large as a sheng measure.

sentences.zh: 自餘多同九真。

translations.literal: The rest were mostly the same as Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Other produce largely matched that of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 海有魚名建同，四足無鱗，鼻如象，吸水上噴，高五六十尺。

translations.literal: In the sea was a fish called Jiantong, with four feet and no scales, its nose like an elephant; it sucked water and spouted it, reaching fifty or sixty chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The sea held a creature called Jiantong — four-legged and scaleless, with an elephant-like snout that spouted water fifty or sixty feet high.

sentences.zh: 有浮胡魚，形似鲠且，嘴如鸚鵡，有八足。

translations.literal: There was a fish called fuhu, shaped like the gengqie fish, its mouth like a parrot, with eight feet.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the fuhu fish, cuttlefish-like, parrot-beaked, with eight tentacles.

sentences.zh: 多大魚，半身出，望之如山。

translations.literal: Great fish were many; half the body emerged, and seen from afar they looked like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Enormous fish often surfaced half out of water, looking from afar like hills.

sentences.zh: 每五六月中，毒氣流行，即以白豬、白牛、羊於城西門外祠之。

translations.literal: Every year in the fifth or sixth month, when poisonous vapors spread, they sacrificed white pigs, white cattle, and sheep outside the west city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the fifth or sixth month, when miasma spread, white pigs, cattle, and sheep were sacrificed outside the west gate.

sentences.zh: 不然，五穀不登，畜多死，人疾疫。

translations.literal: If they did not, the five grains would not ripen, livestock would die in great numbers, and people would suffer pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Without these rites the harvests failed, livestock died in great numbers, and plague struck the people.

sentences.zh: 近都有陵伽缽婆山，上有神祠，每以兵二千人守衛之。

translations.literal: Near the capital was Lingjiabopo mountain; on it was a spirit shrine, guarded each time by two thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Near the capital stood Mount Lingjiabopo, with a spirit shrine guarded by two thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 城東神名婆多利，祭用人肉。

translations.literal: East of the city was a spirit called Batuoli; sacrifices used human flesh.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city was a deity called Batuoli, to whom human-flesh offerings were made.

sentences.zh: 其王年別殺人，以夜祠禱，亦有守衛者千人。

translations.literal: Every year the king separately killed people for nocturnal sacrificial prayer; there were also a thousand guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the king sacrificed human victims in nocturnal rites, also guarded by a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 其敬鬼如此。

translations.literal: Their reverence for ghosts was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was their devotion to spirits.

sentences.zh: 多奉佛法，尤信道士。

translations.literal: They mostly followed Buddhist law and especially trusted Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: They mostly followed Buddhism and especially revered Brahmin priests.

sentences.zh: 佛及道士，並立像於其館。

translations.literal: Both Buddha and Daoist priests had images set up in their halls.
translations.idiomatic: Images of the Buddha and Brahmin priests were erected in their halls.

sentences.zh: 隋大業十二年，遣使貢獻，帝禮之甚厚，於後亦絕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye of Sui they sent envoys with tribute; the emperor treated them very generously, but afterward tribute also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Daye year 12 they sent tribute envoys; the emperor received them lavishly, but contact later ceased.

sentences.zh: 婆利國，自交趾浮海，南過赤土、丹丹，乃至其國。

translations.literal: The state of Poli — from Jiaozhi one floated on the sea, passing south beyond Chi Tu and Dandan, until reaching that state.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Poli, Bali, lay south of Jiaozhi by sea, beyond Chi Tu and Dandan.

sentences.zh: 國界，東西四月行，南北四十五日行。

translations.literal: The state's borders: east to west, four months' travel; north to south, forty-five days' travel.
translations.idiomatic: Its borders measured four months' travel east to west and forty-five days north to south.

sentences.zh: 王姓刹利邪伽，名護濫那婆。

translations.literal: The king's surname was Kshatriyajia; his name was Hulannapo.
translations.idiomatic: The king belonged to the Kshatriya clan and was named Hulannapo.

sentences.zh: 官曰獨訶邪拿，次曰獨訶氏拿。

translations.literal: The chief office was called Dukhiyana; the next rank was Dukhesana.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister was called Dukhiyana; the next in rank was Dukhesana.

sentences.zh: 國人善投輪，其大如鏡，中有竅，外鋒如鋸，遠以投人，無不中。

translations.literal: The people were skilled at throwing wheels; they were as large as mirrors, with a hole in the center, outer edges sharp like saws; thrown from afar at people, none missed.
translations.idiomatic: The people excelled at hurling chakras — mirror-sized discs with a central hole and saw-toothed rims that never missed their mark at range.

sentences.zh: 其餘兵器，與中國略同，俗類真臘，物產同于林邑。

translations.literal: The rest of their weapons were largely the same as China's; customs resembled Zhenla; products were the same as Linyi's.
translations.idiomatic: Other weapons resembled China's; customs resembled Khmer ways; products matched those of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 其殺人及盜，截其手；

translations.literal: For murder and theft they cut off the hand;
translations.idiomatic: Murder and theft were punished by severing the hand;

sentences.zh: 奸者，鎖其足，期年而止。

translations.literal: For adultery they shackled the feet, for one year then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: adultery by shackling the feet for one year.

sentences.zh: 祭祀必以月晦，盤貯酒肴，浮之流水。

translations.literal: Sacrifices were always on the last day of the month; a tray stored wine and food, which was floated on flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were always held on the last day of the month, with trays of food and wine set adrift on the water.

sentences.zh: 每十一月必設大祭。

translations.literal: Every eleventh month a great sacrifice was invariably held.
translations.idiomatic: A great festival was held every eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 海出珊瑚。

translations.literal: The sea produced coral.
translations.idiomatic: Coral came from the sea.

sentences.zh: 有鳥名舍利，解人語。

translations.literal: There was a bird called Sheli that understood human speech.
translations.idiomatic: A bird called Sheli could understand human speech.

sentences.zh: 隋大業十二年，遣使朝貢，後遂絕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye of Sui they sent envoys to pay court with tribute; afterward it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Daye year 12 they sent tribute envoys; contact then ceased.

sentences.zh: 于時南荒有丹丹、盤盤二國，亦來貢方物，其風俗、物產，大抵相類云。

translations.literal: At that time in the southern wilds were the two states of Dandan and Panpan; they also came to present local products; their customs and products were in general similar, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Dandan and Panpan in the southern frontier also sent tribute at that time; their customs and products were broadly similar, it is said.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《禮》云：「南方曰蠻，有不火食者矣。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: The 《Book of Rites》 states: "The south is called Man; there are those who do not cook their food with fire."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: The 《Book of Rites》 states, "The south is called Man; there are those who eat their food uncooked.

sentences.zh: 然其種類非一，與華人錯居，其流曰蜒，曰獽，曰俚，曰獠，曰厓。

translations.literal: Yet their kinds are not one; intermingled with Chinese people they dwell; their branches are called Yan, Rang, Li, Liao, and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their peoples were not one kind. Intermingled with Chinese, their branches included the Yan, Rang, Li, Liao, and Ya.

sentences.zh: 居無君長，隨山洞而居。

translations.literal: They dwelt without lords or chiefs, following mountain caves to reside.
translations.idiomatic: They had no rulers and lived in mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 其俗，斷發文身，好相攻討。

translations.literal: Their custom: cut hair and tattooed bodies; they loved mutually to attack and raid.
translations.idiomatic: They cut their hair and tattooed their bodies and were prone to raiding one another.

sentences.zh: 自秦並三楚，漢平百越，地窮丹徼，景極日南，水陸可居，咸為郡縣。

translations.literal: From Qin annexing the Three Chu, Han pacifying the Baiyue — the land reached to the red frontier, the view extended to Rinan; wherever land and water could be inhabited, all became commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin's annexation of the Three Chu and Han's pacification of the Baiyue, the frontier reached the Red Pass and extended to Rinan; habitable lands along rivers and coasts were all organized into commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 洎乎境分南北，割據各殊，蠻、獠之族，遞為去就。

translations.literal: Down to when the realm was divided into north and south and rival regimes each differed, the Man and Liao peoples alternately came and went.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm split into north and south and rival regimes arose, the Man and Liao peoples shifted their allegiance back and forth.

sentences.zh: 至於林邑、赤土、真臘、婆利則地隔江嶺，莫通中國。

translations.literal: As for Linyi, Chi Tu, Zhenla, and Poli, their lands were separated by rivers and ranges; they did not reach China.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi, Chi Tu, Khmer, and Poli lay beyond rivers and mountain ranges, with no direct contact with China.

sentences.zh: 及隋氏受命，克平九宇，煬帝纂業，威加八荒，甘心遠矣，志求珍異。

translations.literal: When the House of Sui received the Mandate, conquered and pacified the nine realms, Emperor Yang succeeded to the enterprise, his might extended to the eight wilds; his heart delighted in the far; his ambition sought rare and exotic things.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui received the Mandate and pacified the realm, Emperor Yang extended his power to the ends of the earth, his heart set on distant marvels and rare exotic treasures.

sentences.zh: 故師出流求，兵加林邑，威振殊俗，過於秦、漢遠矣。

translations.literal: Therefore troops were dispatched to Liuqiu, arms applied to Linyi; might shook foreign customs — far surpassing Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Hence armies were sent to Liuqiu and Linyi, awe inspiring the outer realms — surpassing Qin and Han by far.

sentences.zh: 雖有荒外之功，無救域中之敗。

translations.literal: Though there was achievement beyond the wilds, it could not save defeat within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: For all their conquests abroad, they could not avert disaster at home.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「非聖人，外甯必有內憂。」

translations.literal: The 《Zuo Zhuan》 says: "One who is not a sage — if outwardly at peace, inwardly must have trouble."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Zuo Zhuan》 says, "One who is not a sage — if at peace abroad, must have trouble within.

sentences.zh: 誠哉斯言也。

translations.literal: Truly so are these words.
translations.idiomatic: How true those words are!

sentences.zh: 大業中，南荒朝貢者十餘國，其事蹟湮滅，今可知者四國而已。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, more than ten states of the southern wilds sent tribute to court; their records are lost to oblivion; of those known today there are only four states.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era more than a dozen southern kingdoms sent tribute, but most of their records are lost — only four are still known today.
